Natural Language Processing · Mini project

Marathi News Intelligence Pipeline

Source code listing

1. Aim

Mini Project based on Real Life NLP Application.

2. Objectives

  • To understand natural language processing and to learn how to apply basic algorithms in this field.
  • To design and implement applications based on natural language processing.

Outcomes: Be able to apply NLP techniques to design real world NLP applications such as machine translation, text categorization, text summarization, information extraction, etc.

3. Hardware / Software Required

LanguagePython 3.10 or newer (the analyser, pipeline, scripts and apps); JavaScript for the in-browser demo engine.
LibrariesPyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, NumPy, pandas, scikit-learn, Streamlit, BeautifulSoup, pytest.
ModelsMahaBERT topic / NER / sentiment / sentence-similarity models (L3Cube, Pune) and NLLB-200 distilled 600M (Meta AI).
DatasetsXL-Sum Marathi (13,627 BBC Marathi articles with summaries), MahaNews (11,721 labelled headlines), and live RSS feeds.
HardwareAny laptop. A GPU (NVIDIA CUDA or Apple Silicon) only makes it faster; developed on a 4 GB RTX 3050 and an Apple Silicon Mac.
OtherA web browser for the single-file demo page; Node.js only for the JavaScript/Python equivalence check.

4. Theory

Natural Language Processing (NLP) is the branch of artificial intelligence that lets computers work with human language. This project applies seven standard NLP tasks to Marathi news, a language with far fewer ready-made tools than English.

4.1 Morphological analysis

Marathi is an agglutinative language: grammatical information is added by joining suffixes to a root, so what English writes as several words becomes one word.

घर        house                       (root)
घरात      = घर + आत          in the house
घरातून    = घर + आतून        from inside the house
घरांमधून  = घर + ां + मधून   from inside the houses
घराच्या   = घर + आ + च्या     of the house

A whitespace tokeniser treats these as five unrelated words, which harms every component that compares words. A morphological analyser reduces each surface form to its root. The analyser here is rule-based: it strips the suffix chain in four ordered layers (clitic, postposition, verb ending, case and number) and then repairs the stem. Length guards count aksharas (written syllables) rather than Unicode code points, because Devanagari vowel signs are separate code points. In the 3,000-article corpus, 36% of tokens carry at least one removable suffix, and normalising them reduces the index vocabulary from 186,593 to 84,480 types (54.7% smaller).

4.2 Information retrieval

BM25 is the standard ranking function for keyword search. A document scores highly when it contains the query terms often (term frequency), when those terms are rare across the collection (inverse document frequency), and it is penalised for length. Dense retrieval instead embeds text as vectors with a neural encoder and ranks by cosine similarity, which can match paraphrases sharing no words. Reciprocal Rank Fusion combines the two ranked lists by rank position rather than by score, because BM25 scores and cosine similarities are on different scales. Ranking quality is reported with recall@k and MRR (mean reciprocal rank).

4.3 Text summarisation

TextRank is an extractive, graph-based method. Sentences are nodes; edges are weighted by TF-IDF cosine similarity; PageRank then scores each sentence by how central it is in that graph. Maximal Marginal Relevance (MMR) selects the final sentences, trading relevance against redundancy so near-duplicates are not all chosen. Summaries are scored with ROUGE, the word overlap with human-written summaries.

4.4 Classification, extraction and sentiment

These three use BERT-family transformer models pre-trained on Marathi (MahaBERT, from L3Cube Pune). Text categorisation predicts one of 12 news topics. Named entity recognition is token classification: each token is labelled as part of a person, location, organisation, date and so on. Sentiment analysis classifies polarity; because the model is trained on short text, it is applied per sentence and aggregated into a document tone. Fine-tuning (training a pre-trained model further on a task's own data) raised topic accuracy from 0.847 to 0.954 on a 3-class benchmark.

4.5 Machine translation

Translation uses NLLB-200, a multilingual sequence-to-sequence transformer, applied sentence by sentence so long inputs stay within its reliable length.

4.6 Knowledge distillation

The browser demo cannot load 700 MB models, so small linear student models were trained to reproduce the large models' outputs over 12,262 articles. Trained on the teacher's probability distributions, they agree with it on 83.0% of topics, 75.7% of sentence sentiment labels and reach F1 0.72 on entities, while fitting in a few megabytes.

4.7 System design

The seven tasks form one pipeline rather than seven programs. The analyser runs first because retrieval, summarisation and entity counting all consume its roots; the enriched articles are then indexed for search. Every claim is measured against a simple baseline, and the negative results are reported alongside the positive ones.

5. Source code

The complete source of the project, in the order the pipeline uses it. Generated files (the built demo page, model weights, downloaded data) are not listed.

  • Configuration and dependencies
    • config.py — Paths, model names, device selection and batch settings.
    • requirements.txt — Python packages the project needs.
  • Core modules — src/
    • src/morph.py — (I) Morphological analyser. Written from scratch; no training data.
    • src/models.py — Lazy, cached loading of every transformer model.
    • src/categorize.py — (D) Topic categorisation into 12 news topics.
    • src/summarize.py — (E) Extractive summarisation: TextRank over a sentence graph, then MMR.
    • src/ner.py — (G) Entity extraction, span repair and alias merging.
    • src/sentiment.py — (F) Sentence, document and per-entity sentiment.
    • src/translate.py — (A) Marathi to English translation with NLLB-200.
    • src/retrieve.py — (C) BM25, dense retrieval and reciprocal rank fusion.
    • src/pipeline.py — Runs every stage over one article.
    • src/ingest.py — Live news ingestion from RSS feeds.
    • src/lite.py — Small in-browser student models used by the demo page.
  • Scripts — scripts/
    • scripts/download_data.py — Downloads the XL-Sum and MahaNews datasets.
    • scripts/build_corpus.py — Runs the pipeline over the corpus.
    • scripts/build_index.py — Builds the BM25 and dense search indexes.
    • scripts/train_classifier.py — Fine-tunes MahaBERT as a topic classifier.
    • scripts/evaluate.py — All experiments, plus a Marathi-aware ROUGE implementation.
    • scripts/distill_label.py — Labels the corpus with the full models, to train the students.
    • scripts/train_lite.py — Trains and scores the in-browser student models.
    • scripts/export_demo.py — Exports the demo page's data.
    • scripts/build_demo_page.py — Assembles the single-file demo page.
    • scripts/verify_demo.py — Checks the page's JavaScript against the Python.
  • Applications — app/
    • app/dashboard.py — Streamlit dashboard.
    • app/server.py — Local model server the demo page can use.
    • app/demo_engine.js — The demo page's NLP engine: a JavaScript port of the modules above.
    • app/demo_template.html — The demo page's layout and interface code.
  • Tests — tests/
    • tests/test_pipeline.py — 51 fast tests plus 8 that load the models.

1# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
2"""
3Rule-based morphological analyser for Marathi (module I of the pipeline).
4
5Marathi is agglutinative and heavily suffixing: a single nominal root takes a
6number suffix, an oblique-stem change, and then one or more postpositions that
7are written joined to the stem:
8
9    घर  (house)
10    घरात      = घर + आत          locative      "in the house"
11    घरातून    = घर + आतून        ablative      "from inside the house"
12    घरांमधून  = घर + ां + मधून   plural + abl. "from inside the houses"
13    घराच्या   = घर + आ(obl) + च्या  genitive
14
15A whitespace tokeniser therefore treats all four as unrelated types, which is
16why plain keyword search performs poorly on Marathi. This module strips the
17suffix chain, undoes the oblique stem change, and returns a normalised root
18plus the morphological features it removed.
19
20The analyser is deliberately rule-based rather than statistical: it needs no
21training data, runs at roughly 100k tokens/sec, and its output is inspectable,
22which is what makes the retrieval ablation in scripts/evaluate.py meaningful.
23
24Design note -- why aksharas, not characters
25-------------------------------------------
26Devanagari vowel signs (matras) are separate Unicode code points, so len() is
27not a measure of how much word is left. "घरा" is three code points but only
28two aksharas (घ + र). Every length guard below therefore counts aksharas,
29otherwise the minimum-stem check fires inconsistently and related forms such
30as शाळा / शाळेत end up with different roots -- which would defeat the whole
31purpose of the analyser.
32"""
33from __future__ import annotations
34
35import re
36import unicodedata
37from dataclasses import dataclass, field
38from functools import lru_cache
39from typing import List, Optional, Tuple
40
41# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
42# Character classes
43# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
44DEVANAGARI = r"ऀ-ॿ"
45_TOKEN_RE = re.compile(rf"[{DEVANAGARI}]+|[A-Za-z]+|\d+")
46_SENT_RE = re.compile(r"(?<=[।\.\!\?])\s+")
47
48VIRAMA = "्"
49
50# Combining marks: anusvara/visarga block, nukta, all vowel signs, virama,
51# accents and vocalic marks. These attach to a base akshara.
52_MARKS = frozenset(
53    [chr(c) for c in range(0x0900, 0x0904)]        # candrabindu, anusvara, visarga
54    + [chr(0x093A), chr(0x093B), chr(0x093C)]      # vowel signs oe/ooe, nukta
55    + [chr(c) for c in range(0x093E, 0x0950)]      # matras + virama
56    + [chr(c) for c in range(0x0951, 0x0958)]      # accents
57    + [chr(0x0962), chr(0x0963)]                   # vocalic l matras
58)
59
60# Vowel signs that may be shed when normalising a stem's final syllable.
61_FINAL_MATRAS = frozenset("ािीुूृेैोौ")
62
63
64def akshara_len(s: str) -> int:
65    """Number of base characters, ignoring combining vowel signs and virama."""
66    return sum(1 for ch in s if ch not in _MARKS)
67
68

76# Layers are stripped from the outside in:

138# Derivational suffixes are NOT part of the default chain: stripping कार off

141DERIVATIONAL = [
142    ("पणा", "NMLZ"), ("त्व", "NMLZ"), ("कार", "AGT"),
143    ("वाला", "AGT"), ("गिरी", "NMLZ"), ("दार", "AGT"),
144]

147def _norm_table(table) -> List[Tuple[str, str, str]]:
148    """Pad 2-tuples with an empty replacement and sort longest-match-first."""
149    out = [(t[0], t[1], t[2] if len(t) > 2 else "") for t in table]
150    return sorted(out, key=lambda kv: -len(kv[0]))
151
152
153_LAYERS = [
154    ("clitic", _norm_table(CLITICS)),
155    ("postp", _norm_table(POSTPOSITIONS)),
156    ("verb", _norm_table(VERB_SUFFIXES)),
157    ("case", _norm_table(CASE_NUMBER)),
158]
159_DERIV_LAYER = ("deriv", _norm_table(DERIVATIONAL))
160
161MIN_STEM = 2          # minimum aksharas that must survive a strip
162MIN_DERIV_STEM = 3    # derivation needs a longer residue to be plausible
163MAX_STRIPS = 4        # guard against runaway peeling

189@dataclass
190class Analysis:
191    """Result of analysing a single surface token."""
192    surface: str
193    root: str
194    features: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)
195    stripped: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)
196
197    @property
198    def is_inflected(self) -> bool:
199        return bool(self.stripped)
200
201    def __str__(self) -> str:
202        feats = "+".join(self.features) if self.features else "-"
203        return f"{self.surface} -> {self.root} [{feats}]"
204
205
206# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
207# Stem restoration
208# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
209def _restore_stem(stem_form: str) -> str:
210    """
211    Normalise the stem left behind after suffix removal.
212
213    The oblique stem of a consonant-final noun ends in -ा (घर -> घरा-), and
214    plural/oblique forms surface with -े or -ी. Shedding one final vowel sign
215    -- as long as two aksharas remain -- collapses घर / घरा / घरे, and
216    शाळा / शाळे, onto a single root.
217    """
218    if not stem_form:
219        return stem_form
220
221    # A dangling virama is never a valid word end (पुण्य- from पुण्यात).
222    while stem_form.endswith(VIRAMA):
223        stem_form = stem_form[:-1]
224
225    if stem_form and stem_form[-1] in _FINAL_MATRAS and akshara_len(stem_form) >= MIN_STEM:
226        stem_form = stem_form[:-1]
227
228    return stem_form
229
230
231def _strip_once(word: str, layers) -> Optional[Tuple[str, str, str]]:
232    """Remove at most one suffix. Returns (stem, suffix, feature) or None."""
233    for layer_name, table in layers:
234        floor = MIN_DERIV_STEM if layer_name == "deriv" else MIN_STEM
235        for suf, feat, repl in table:
236            if not word.endswith(suf):
237                continue
238            candidate = word[: -len(suf)] + repl
239            if akshara_len(candidate) >= floor:
240                return candidate, suf, feat
241    return None
242
243
244@lru_cache(maxsize=200_000)
245def analyse(word: str, derivational: bool = False) -> Analysis:
246    """Analyse one token into root + morphological features."""
247    surface = word
248    word = unicodedata.normalize("NFC", word)
249
250    if surface in EXCEPTIONS:
251        return Analysis(surface=surface, root=EXCEPTIONS[surface])
252
253    layers = _LAYERS + [_DERIV_LAYER] if derivational else _LAYERS
254    feats: List[str] = []
255    strips: List[str] = []
256
257    for _ in range(MAX_STRIPS):
258        hit = _strip_once(word, layers)
259        if hit is None:
260            break
261        new_stem, suf, feat = hit
262        word = new_stem
263        feats.append(feat)
264        strips.append(suf)
265
266    root = _restore_stem(word)
267    return Analysis(surface=surface, root=root, features=feats, stripped=strips)
268
269
270def stem(word: str) -> str:
271    """Convenience wrapper: surface form -> normalised root."""
272    return analyse(word).root
273
274
275# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
276# Tokenisation helpers used by the rest of the pipeline
277# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
278def tokenize(text: str) -> List[str]:
279    """Script-aware word tokeniser (Devanagari, Latin, digits)."""
280    return _TOKEN_RE.findall(text or "")
281
282
283def sent_tokenize(text: str) -> List[str]:
284    """Split on danda and western sentence punctuation."""
285    parts = _SENT_RE.split((text or "").strip())
286    return [p.strip() for p in parts if p and p.strip()]
287
288
289def normalize_tokens(text: str, *, use_morph: bool = True,
290                     drop_stopwords: bool = True) -> List[str]:
291    """
292    Full normalisation path used for indexing and similarity.
293
294    `use_morph=False` reproduces the plain-tokenisation baseline, which is what
295    the retrieval ablation compares against.
296    """
297    out = []
298    for tok in tokenize(text):
299        if drop_stopwords and tok in STOPWORDS:
300            continue
301        t = stem(tok) if use_morph else tok
302        if drop_stopwords and t in STOPWORDS:
303            continue
304        if akshara_len(t) >= MIN_STEM or t.isascii():
305            out.append(t)
306    return out
307

318    ]

323    groups = [

Lazy, cached loading of every transformer model.

1# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
2"""
3Lazy, cached model loading.
4
5Every model in this project is loaded through here so that (a) the Streamlit
6app and the batch scripts share one copy per process, and (b) a 4 GB laptop
7GPU does not end up holding five models at once. Models are moved to the GPU
8on first use and kept in fp16 there; CPU stays fp32 because fp16 matmul on CPU
9is slower, not faster.
10"""
11from __future__ import annotations
12
13import functools
14import sys
15from pathlib import Path
16
17import torch
18
19sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent))
20import config  # noqa: E402
21
22
23def _prepare(model):
24    model.eval()
25    if config.DEVICE == "cuda":
26        model = model.half().to("cuda")
27    elif config.DEVICE != "cpu":
28        model = model.to(config.DEVICE)
29    return model
30
31
32@functools.lru_cache(maxsize=None)
33def load_classifier(name: str):
34    """Sequence-classification model + tokenizer (topic, sentiment)."""
35    from transformers import AutoModelForSequenceClassification, AutoTokenizer
36    tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(name)
37    mod = _prepare(AutoModelForSequenceClassification.from_pretrained(name))
38    return tok, mod
39
40
41@functools.lru_cache(maxsize=None)
42def load_token_classifier(name: str):
43    """Token-classification model + tokenizer (NER)."""
44    from transformers import AutoModelForTokenClassification, AutoTokenizer
45    tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(name)
46    mod = _prepare(AutoModelForTokenClassification.from_pretrained(name))
47    return tok, mod
48
49
50@functools.lru_cache(maxsize=None)
51def load_encoder(name: str = config.MODEL_SBERT):
52    """Bare encoder for sentence embeddings (mean pooling applied by caller)."""
53    from transformers import AutoModel, AutoTokenizer
54    tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(name)
55    mod = _prepare(AutoModel.from_pretrained(name))
56    return tok, mod
57
58
59@functools.lru_cache(maxsize=None)
60def load_translator(name: str = config.MODEL_TRANSLATE):
61    """Seq2seq translation model (NLLB-200 distilled)."""
62    from transformers import AutoModelForSeq2SeqLM, AutoTokenizer
63    tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(name, src_lang=config.NLLB_SRC_LANG)
64    mod = _prepare(AutoModelForSeq2SeqLM.from_pretrained(name))
65    # NLLB ships generation_config.max_length=200, which clashes with the
66    # max_new_tokens we pass and prints a warning on every batch.
67    mod.generation_config.max_length = None
68    return tok, mod
69
70
71def free():
72    """Drop every cached model and empty the CUDA allocator."""
73    for fn in (load_classifier, load_token_classifier, load_encoder,
74               load_translator):
75        fn.cache_clear()
76    if torch.cuda.is_available():
77        torch.cuda.empty_cache()
78    elif config.DEVICE == "mps":
79        torch.mps.empty_cache()
80
81
82@torch.no_grad()
83def embed(texts, name: str = config.MODEL_SBERT, batch_size: int = None,
84          show_progress: bool = False):
85    """
86    Mean-pooled, L2-normalised sentence embeddings.
87
88    Implemented directly on top of transformers rather than pulling in
89    sentence-transformers, which keeps the dependency list short and avoids a
90    version pin against transformers 5.x.
91    """
92    import numpy as np
93    tok, mod = load_encoder(name)
94    bs = batch_size or config.BATCH_SIZE
95    texts = [t if t else " " for t in texts]
96    out = []
97
98    for i in range(0, len(texts), bs):
99        chunk = texts[i:i + bs]
100        enc = tok(chunk, padding=True, truncation=True,
101                  max_length=config.MAX_LEN, return_tensors="pt").to(config.DEVICE)
102        hidden = mod(**enc).last_hidden_state              # (B, T, H)
103        mask = enc["attention_mask"].unsqueeze(-1).to(hidden.dtype)
104        pooled = (hidden * mask).sum(1) / mask.sum(1).clamp(min=1e-9)
105        pooled = torch.nn.functional.normalize(pooled, p=2, dim=1)
106        out.append(pooled.float().cpu().numpy())
107        if show_progress and (i // bs) % 20 == 0:
108            print(f"    embedded {min(i + bs, len(texts))}/{len(texts)}", flush=True)
109
110    return np.vstack(out) if out else np.zeros((0, 768), dtype="float32")

1# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
2"""
3Topic categorisation (module D).
4
5Two backends:
6
7  * `l3cube-pune/marathi-topic-all-doc` -- 12-way MahaNews document classifier,
8    used out of the box so the pipeline works with no training step.
9  * a locally fine-tuned MahaBERT head produced by scripts/train_classifier.py,
10    selected with MNIP_TOPIC_MODEL=custom. It is NOT the default -- see
11    active_model() for why a better benchmark score would make the pipeline
12    worse.
13
14Both expose the same `classify()` signature so callers do not care which one
15is active.
16"""
17from __future__ import annotations
18
19import os
20import sys
21from dataclasses import dataclass
22from pathlib import Path
23from typing import List
24

32@dataclass
33class TopicPrediction:
34    label: str
35    score: float
36    all_scores: dict
37
38
39def active_model() -> str:
40    """
41    The model the pipeline uses by default.
42
43    This deliberately stays on the 12-class topic model even after
44    scripts/train_classifier.py has produced a fine-tuned checkpoint. The
45    fine-tuned head is trained on MahaNews, whose label space is only
46    entertainment / sports / state -- it scores better *on that benchmark*
47    (0.954 vs 0.847) precisely because it answers an easier question. Letting
48    it take over the pipeline would collapse Politics, Tech, Health, Crime and
49    the rest into "state" and make every downstream view worse.
50
51    Set MNIP_TOPIC_MODEL=custom to use the fine-tuned head, which is what the
52    classification experiment in scripts/evaluate.py does.
53    """
54    choice = os.environ.get("MNIP_TOPIC_MODEL", "").lower()
55    if choice in ("custom", "finetuned", "local"):
56        if (config.CUSTOM_TOPIC_DIR / "config.json").exists():
57            return str(config.CUSTOM_TOPIC_DIR)
58        raise FileNotFoundError(
59            f"MNIP_TOPIC_MODEL={choice} but no checkpoint at "
60            f"{config.CUSTOM_TOPIC_DIR}. Run scripts/train_classifier.py first.")
61    return config.MODEL_TOPIC
62
63
64def custom_model_available() -> bool:
65    return (config.CUSTOM_TOPIC_DIR / "config.json").exists()

68@torch.no_grad()
69def classify(texts: List[str], model_name: str = None,
70             batch_size: int = None) -> List[TopicPrediction]:
71    """Classify a batch of documents into news topics."""
72    if isinstance(texts, str):
73        texts = [texts]
74    model_name = model_name or active_model()
75    tok, mod = models.load_classifier(model_name)
76    id2label = mod.config.id2label
77    bs = batch_size or config.BATCH_SIZE
78    results: List[TopicPrediction] = []
79
80    for i in range(0, len(texts), bs):
81        chunk = [t if t else " " for t in texts[i:i + bs]]
82        enc = tok(chunk, padding=True, truncation=True,
83                  max_length=config.MAX_LEN, return_tensors="pt").to(config.DEVICE)
84        probs = mod(**enc).logits.float().softmax(-1).cpu()
85        for row in probs:
86            idx = int(row.argmax())
87            results.append(TopicPrediction(
88                label=id2label[idx],
89                score=float(row[idx]),
90                all_scores={id2label[j]: float(row[j]) for j in range(len(row))},
91            ))
92    return results
93

(E) Extractive summarisation: TextRank over a sentence graph, then MMR.

1# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
2"""
3Extractive summarisation (module E).
4
5Two scorers, both of which rank sentences and then de-duplicate with MMR:
6
7  * `textrank`  -- PageRank over a sentence-similarity graph built from
8                   morphologically normalised TF-IDF vectors. No neural model,
9                   so it runs on CPU in milliseconds.
10  * `embedding` -- the same graph but with MahaBERT-SBERT sentence vectors,
11                   which catches paraphrase that shares no surface tokens.
12
13A `lead` baseline (first k sentences) is included because for news it is a
14genuinely strong baseline, and the evaluation script reports all three so the
15comparison is honest rather than flattering.
16
17Morphology matters here: without it, "सरकारने" and "सरकारच्या" contribute to
18different TF-IDF dimensions and two sentences about the same subject look
19unrelated.
20"""
21from __future__ import annotations
22
23import sys
24from dataclasses import dataclass
25from pathlib import Path
26from typing import List
27
28import numpy as np
29
30sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent))
31from src.morph import normalize_tokens, sent_tokenize  # noqa: E402
32
33DAMPING = 0.85
34MAX_ITER = 100
35TOL = 1e-6
36
37
38@dataclass
39class Summary:
40    sentences: List[str]
41    indices: List[int]
42    method: str
43
44    @property
45    def text(self) -> str:
46        return " ".join(self.sentences)
47
48
49# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
50# Similarity graphs
51# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
52def _tfidf_matrix(sentences: List[str]) -> np.ndarray:
53    """Morphologically normalised TF-IDF, built without sklearn's tokenizer."""
54    docs = [normalize_tokens(s) for s in sentences]
55    vocab = {}
56    for d in docs:
57        for t in d:
58            vocab.setdefault(t, len(vocab))
59    if not vocab:
60        return np.zeros((len(sentences), 1), dtype="float64")
61
62    # float64 so the page's JavaScript port (always float64) ranks identically.
63    tf = np.zeros((len(docs), len(vocab)), dtype="float64")
64    for i, d in enumerate(docs):
65        for t in d:
66            tf[i, vocab[t]] += 1.0
67    tf /= np.maximum(tf.sum(1, keepdims=True), 1e-9)
68
69    df = (tf > 0).sum(0)
70    idf = np.log((1 + len(docs)) / (1 + df)) + 1.0
71    return tf * idf
72
73
74def _cosine_graph(vectors: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
75    norms = np.linalg.norm(vectors, axis=1, keepdims=True)
76    unit = vectors / np.maximum(norms, 1e-9)
77    sim = unit @ unit.T
78    np.fill_diagonal(sim, 0.0)
79    return np.clip(sim, 0.0, None)
80
81
82def _pagerank(sim: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
83    """Power iteration; falls back to uniform scores on a disconnected graph."""
84    n = sim.shape[0]
85    if n == 0:
86        return np.zeros(0)
87    row = sim.sum(1, keepdims=True)
88    # Dangling rows get a uniform transition so probability mass is conserved.
89    transition = np.where(row > 0, sim / np.maximum(row, 1e-9), 1.0 / n)
90    scores = np.full(n, 1.0 / n)
91    for _ in range(MAX_ITER):
92        nxt = (1 - DAMPING) / n + DAMPING * (transition.T @ scores)
93        if np.abs(nxt - scores).sum() < TOL:
94            return nxt
95        scores = nxt
96    return scores
97
98
99def _mmr(order: List[int], sim: np.ndarray, k: int,
100         lambda_: float = 0.7) -> List[int]:
101    """
102    Greedily pick k sentences trading relevance against redundancy.
103
104    Relevance is fixed up front from each sentence's PageRank position, not
105    recomputed against the shrinking candidate list -- otherwise a sentence's
106    relevance rises simply because better ones were already taken, and the
107    redundancy penalty stops being comparable across iterations.
108    """
109    n = max(len(order), 1)
110    relevance = {idx: 1.0 - pos / n for pos, idx in enumerate(order)}
111
112    selected: List[int] = []
113    candidates = list(order)
114    while candidates and len(selected) < k:
115        best, best_score = None, -np.inf
116        for idx in candidates:
117            redundancy = max((sim[idx, j] for j in selected), default=0.0)
118            score = round(lambda_ * relevance[idx] - (1 - lambda_) * redundancy, 12)
119            if score > best_score:
120                best, best_score = idx, score
121        selected.append(best)
122        candidates.remove(best)
123    return selected
124
125
126# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
127# Public API
128# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
129def summarize(text: str, k: int = 3, method: str = "textrank",
130              lambda_: float = 0.7) -> Summary:
131    """Return the k most representative sentences, in original order."""
132    sentences = [s for s in sent_tokenize(text) if len(s.split()) >= 3]
133    if not sentences:
134        return Summary(sentences=[], indices=[], method=method)
135    if len(sentences) <= k:
136        return Summary(sentences=sentences, indices=list(range(len(sentences))),
137                       method=method)
138
139    if method == "lead":
140        idx = list(range(k))
141        return Summary(sentences=[sentences[i] for i in idx], indices=idx,
142                       method=method)
143
144    if method == "embedding":
145        from src import models
146        vectors = models.embed(sentences)
147    else:
148        vectors = _tfidf_matrix(sentences)
149
150    sim = _cosine_graph(vectors)
151    # Scores are rounded before a stable sort so that exact ties (repeated
152    # sentences are common in news) keep document order. Without the rounding
153    # the order of a tie depends on last-bit floating-point noise, which
154    # differs between numpy and the page's JavaScript port.
155    ranked = [int(i) for i in np.argsort(-np.round(_pagerank(sim), 12), kind="stable")]
156    chosen = sorted(_mmr(ranked, sim, k, lambda_))
157    return Summary(sentences=[sentences[i] for i in chosen], indices=chosen,
158                   method=method)
159
160
161def summarize_many(texts: List[str], k: int = 3,
162                   method: str = "textrank") -> List[Summary]:
163    return [summarize(t, k=k, method=method) for t in texts]
164
165
166if __name__ == "__main__":
167    import json
168    sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8")
169    import config
170    row = json.loads(open(config.XLSUM_TEST, encoding="utf-8").readline())
171    print("TITLE  :", row["title"])
172    print("GOLD   :", row["summary"][:220])

174        s = summarize(row["text"], k=2, method=m)
175        print(f"\n{m.upper():8s}:", s.text[:300])

(G) Entity extraction, span repair and alias merging.

1# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
2"""
3Named-entity / information extraction (module G).
4
5Uses `l3cube-pune/marathi-ner` (MahaNER). Note that this model emits *flat*
6labels -- Person, Location, Organization, Date, Time, Measure, Designation,
7Other -- with no B-/I- prefixes. Consecutive wordpieces carrying the same
8label therefore have to be merged into spans here, and because there is no
9B- tag two adjacent distinct entities of the same type are indistinguishable;
10we accept that and merge them, which is the standard reading of this tagset.
11
12Spans are recovered through the tokenizer's offset mapping so the surface text
13is taken verbatim from the input rather than rebuilt from wordpieces (which
14would lose the original spacing and mangle Devanagari conjuncts).
15"""
16from __future__ import annotations
17
18import sys
19from collections import Counter, defaultdict
20from dataclasses import dataclass
21from pathlib import Path
22from typing import Dict, List
23
24import torch
25
26sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent))
27import config                      # noqa: E402
28from src import models             # noqa: E402
29from src.morph import stem as morph_stem  # noqa: E402
30
31# Types worth surfacing in the dashboard; Measure/Time/Other are kept out of
32# the entity summary but still returned by extract().
33HEADLINE_TYPES = ("Person", "Organization", "Location", "Date", "Designation")
34
35
36@dataclass
37class Entity:
38    text: str
39    label: str
40    start: int
41    end: int
42    score: float
43
44    @property
45    def canonical(self) -> str:
46        """
47        Case-stripped form used to aggregate mentions across the corpus.
48
49        Marathi declines proper nouns like any other noun -- मुंबई / मुंबईत /
50        मुंबईतील are the same place, and भारतीय जनता पक्षाच्या is the same
51        party as भारतीय जनता पक्ष. Counting surface forms would scatter one
52        entity across half a dozen rows, so the analyser (module I) is applied
53        to the final token, which is the one that carries the case suffix.
54        """
55        parts = self.text.split()
56        if not parts:
57            return self.text
58        return " ".join(parts[:-1] + [morph_stem(parts[-1])]).strip()
59
60    def __str__(self) -> str:
61        return f"{self.text} ({self.label}, {self.score:.2f})"
62
63
64# Characters that end a word. Anything else (including Devanagari combining
65# marks) is treated as word-internal.
66_BOUNDARY = set(" \t\n\r " + "।,.;:!?\"'()[]{}<>%/\\|-–—")
67
68
69def _snap_to_word(text: str, start: int, end: int) -> tuple:
70    """
71    Widen a span to whole-word boundaries.
72
73    Wordpiece tokenisers happily split a Devanagari word between a consonant
74    and its vowel sign, so a span can begin at a combining mark -- which is how
75    पंतप्रधान came back as ंतप्रधान. Snapping outwards to the nearest
76    boundary character restores the full orthographic word.
77    """
78    while start > 0 and text[start - 1] not in _BOUNDARY:
79        start -= 1
80    while end < len(text) and text[end] not in _BOUNDARY:
81        end += 1
82    return start, end
83
84
85@torch.no_grad()
86def extract(text: str, max_length: int = None) -> List[Entity]:
87    """Extract entities from a single document."""
88    if not text or not text.strip():
89        return []
90
91    tok, mod = models.load_token_classifier(config.MODEL_NER)
92    id2label = mod.config.id2label
93    max_length = max_length or config.MAX_LEN
94
95    enc = tok(text, return_offsets_mapping=True, truncation=True,
96              max_length=max_length, return_tensors="pt")
97    offsets = enc.pop("offset_mapping")[0].tolist()
98    enc.pop("special_tokens_mask", None)
99    enc = {k: v.to(config.DEVICE) for k, v in enc.items()}
100
101    probs = mod(**enc).logits.float().softmax(-1)[0].cpu()
102    label_ids = probs.argmax(-1).tolist()
103    scores = probs.max(-1).values.tolist()
104
105    spans: List[Entity] = []
106    cur = None
107    for (start, end), lid, sc in zip(offsets, label_ids, scores):
108        if start == end:                      # special token
109            continue
110        label = id2label[lid]
111        if label == "Other":
112            cur = None
113            continue
114        # Continue the current span when the label matches and the gap is only
115        # whitespace; otherwise start a new one.
116        if cur and cur.label == label and start - cur.end <= 1:
117            cur.end = end
118            cur.score = (cur.score + sc) / 2
119        else:
120            cur = Entity(text="", label=label, start=start, end=end, score=sc)
121            spans.append(cur)
122
123    for sp in spans:
124        sp.start, sp.end = _snap_to_word(text, sp.start, sp.end)
125        sp.text = text[sp.start:sp.end].strip()
126
127    # Snapping can make two adjacent spans of the same type identical; collapse
128    # runs of duplicates while preserving order.
129    deduped: List[Entity] = []
130    for sp in spans:
131        if not sp.text:
132            continue
133        if deduped and deduped[-1].text == sp.text and deduped[-1].label == sp.label:
134            continue
135        deduped.append(sp)
136    return deduped
137
138
139def extract_many(texts: List[str]) -> List[List[Entity]]:
140    return [extract(t) for t in texts]
141
142
143def summarize_entities(entities: List[Entity]) -> Dict[str, List[str]]:
144    """
145    Group entities by type, de-duplicated and ordered by frequency.
146
147    Mentions are *grouped* by their canonical (de-inflected) form so that
148    मुंबई and मुंबईत count as one entity, but each group is *displayed* using
149    its most frequent surface form -- de-inflection is a good equivalence key
150    and a poor label, since it turns शिंदे into शिंद.
151    """
152    counts: Dict[tuple, int] = Counter()
153    surfaces: Dict[tuple, Counter] = defaultdict(Counter)
154    for e in entities:
155        key = (e.label, e.canonical)
156        counts[key] += 1
157        surfaces[key][e.text] += 1
158
159    buckets: Dict[str, List[str]] = defaultdict(list)
160    for (label, _canon), _n in counts.most_common():
161        buckets[label].append(surfaces[(label, _canon)].most_common(1)[0][0])
162    return dict(buckets)
163
164
165def merge_aliases(counts: Counter, min_parts: int = 2,
166                  host_ratio: float = 0.5) -> Counter:
167    """
168    Fold short-form mentions into the full name they abbreviate.
169
170    News text alternates between नरेंद्र मोदी and plain मोदी, and counting
171    them separately splits one person across two rows in the corpus-level
172    tallies. A single-token name is merged into a multi-token name that ends
173    with it, provided the long form is at least `host_ratio` as frequent as
174    the short one. That threshold keeps a genuinely common surname from being
175    absorbed into some rare full name that happens to share it, while still
176    merging the ordinary case where both forms are used about equally often
177    (ट्रंप 40 / डोनाल्ड ट्रंप 39).
178
179    Deliberately conservative: it does not touch initials, honorifics or
180    nicknames, and it never merges two multi-token names. Real coreference
181    would need a dedicated model; this only fixes the one pattern that
182    dominates the counts.
183    """
184    merged = Counter(counts)
185    longs = [n for n in counts if len(n.split()) >= min_parts]
186    for short, n_short in list(counts.items()):
187        if len(short.split()) != 1:
188            continue
189        hosts = [L for L in longs if L.split()[-1] == short]
190        if not hosts:
191            continue
192        host = max(hosts, key=lambda L: counts[L])
193        if counts[host] >= host_ratio * n_short:
194            merged[host] += n_short
195            del merged[short]
196    return merged
197
198
199if __name__ == "__main__":
200    sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8")
201    demo = ("मुख्यमंत्री एकनाथ शिंदे यांनी सोमवारी मुंबईत भारतीय जनता पक्षाच्या "
202            "बैठकीत नवीन योजनेची घोषणा केली. ही योजना १ जानेवारी २०२४ पासून "
203            "लागू होणार आहे.")
204    ents = extract(demo)
205    for e in ents:
206        print("  ", e)
207    print("\n  grouped:", summarize_entities(ents))

1# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
2"""
3Sentiment analysis (module F).
4
5`l3cube-pune/marathi-sentiment-md` is a 3-way Negative/Neutral/Positive model
6trained on tweet-length Marathi text, so it is applied per sentence rather
7than to a whole article; document tone is then the length-weighted mean of the
8sentence polarities. This also gives the per-entity tone used by the
9dashboard: the sentiment of an entity is the mean polarity of the sentences it
10appears in.
11"""
12from __future__ import annotations
13
14import sys
15from collections import defaultdict
16from dataclasses import dataclass, field
17from pathlib import Path
18from typing import Dict, List
19
20import torch
21
22sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent))
23import config                      # noqa: E402
24from src import models             # noqa: E402
25from src.morph import sent_tokenize  # noqa: E402
26
27# Maps the model's classes onto a scalar polarity in [-1, 1].
28POLARITY = {"Negative": -1.0, "Neutral": 0.0, "Positive": 1.0}
29
30
31@dataclass
32class SentenceSentiment:
33    text: str
34    label: str
35    score: float
36    polarity: float
37
38
39@dataclass
40class DocSentiment:
41    label: str
42    polarity: float
43    sentences: List[SentenceSentiment] = field(default_factory=list)
44
45    @property
46    def distribution(self) -> Dict[str, int]:
47        d = {"Negative": 0, "Neutral": 0, "Positive": 0}
48        for s in self.sentences:
49            d[s.label] = d.get(s.label, 0) + 1
50        return d
51
52
53def _label_from_polarity(p: float) -> str:
54    if p > 0.15:
55        return "Positive"
56    if p < -0.15:
57        return "Negative"
58    return "Neutral"
59
60
61@torch.no_grad()
62def classify_sentences(sentences: List[str],
63                       batch_size: int = None) -> List[SentenceSentiment]:
64    """Polarity of each sentence."""
65    if not sentences:
66        return []
67    tok, mod = models.load_classifier(config.MODEL_SENTIMENT)
68    id2label = mod.config.id2label
69    bs = batch_size or config.BATCH_SIZE
70    out: List[SentenceSentiment] = []
71
72    for i in range(0, len(sentences), bs):
73        chunk = [s if s else " " for s in sentences[i:i + bs]]
74        enc = tok(chunk, padding=True, truncation=True,
75                  max_length=config.MAX_LEN, return_tensors="pt").to(config.DEVICE)
76        probs = mod(**enc).logits.float().softmax(-1).cpu()
77        for text, row in zip(chunk, probs):
78            idx = int(row.argmax())
79            label = id2label[idx]
80            # Expected polarity rather than the argmax class: keeps a
81            # 0.51/0.49 Negative/Neutral sentence from counting as strongly
82            # negative when averaged over a document.
83            pol = sum(POLARITY[id2label[j]] * float(row[j]) for j in range(len(row)))
84            out.append(SentenceSentiment(text=text, label=label,
85                                         score=float(row[idx]), polarity=pol))
86    return out
87
88
89def analyse_document(text: str) -> DocSentiment:
90    """Length-weighted document tone built from sentence-level polarity."""
91    sents = sent_tokenize(text)
92    if not sents:
93        return DocSentiment(label="Neutral", polarity=0.0)
94    scored = classify_sentences(sents)
95    weights = [max(len(s.text), 1) for s in scored]
96    total = sum(weights)
97    pol = sum(s.polarity * w for s, w in zip(scored, weights)) / total
98    return DocSentiment(label=_label_from_polarity(pol), polarity=pol,
99                        sentences=scored)
100
101
102def entity_sentiment(doc: DocSentiment, entities) -> Dict[str, float]:
103    """
104    Mean polarity of the sentences each entity is mentioned in.
105
106    This is what answers "how is politician X being covered this month" once
107    aggregated across the corpus.
108    """
109    scores: Dict[str, List[float]] = defaultdict(list)
110    for sent in doc.sentences:
111        for ent in entities:
112            if ent.text and ent.text in sent.text:
113                scores[ent.text].append(sent.polarity)
114    return {k: sum(v) / len(v) for k, v in scores.items() if v}
115
116
117if __name__ == "__main__":
118    sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8")
119    demo = ("भारतीय संघाने शानदार विजय मिळवला आणि चाहत्यांनी जल्लोष केला. "
120            "मात्र दुखापतीमुळे कर्णधार पुढील सामन्याला मुकणार आहे. "
121            "सामना मुंबईत खेळवण्यात आला.")
122    d = analyse_document(demo)
123    print(f"  document: {d.label}  polarity={d.polarity:+.3f}  {d.distribution}")
124    for s in d.sentences:
125        print(f"    [{s.label:8s} {s.polarity:+.2f}] {s.text[:60]}")

1# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
2"""
3Marathi -> English machine translation (module A).
4
5Uses NLLB-200 (distilled, 600M). Two jobs in this pipeline:
6
7  1. Render Marathi summaries and headlines for a non-Marathi reader.
8  2. Provide the cross-lingual query path -- an English query is *not*
9     translated at search time; instead documents carry an English rendering
10     of their summary, which the retriever can match against. Translating the
11     corpus once is far cheaper than translating every query and gives the
12     user something readable in the results.
13
14Long inputs are split on sentence boundaries and translated in batches, since
15NLLB degrades badly past its training length.
16"""
17from __future__ import annotations
18
19import sys
20from pathlib import Path
21from typing import List
22
23import torch
24
25sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent))
26import config                      # noqa: E402
27from src import models             # noqa: E402
28from src.morph import sent_tokenize  # noqa: E402
29
30
31def _target_lang_id(tok) -> int:
32    """
33    Resolve the forced BOS token for the target language.
34
35    transformers moved this around across versions: `lang_code_to_id` was
36    removed in 5.x, so fall back to a plain vocabulary lookup.
37    """
38    code = config.NLLB_TGT_LANG
39    mapping = getattr(tok, "lang_code_to_id", None)
40    if isinstance(mapping, dict) and code in mapping:
41        return mapping[code]
42    tid = tok.convert_tokens_to_ids(code)
43    if tid is None or tid == tok.unk_token_id:
44        raise ValueError(f"Could not resolve NLLB language token {code!r}")
45    return tid
46
47
48@torch.no_grad()
49def translate(texts, max_new_tokens: int = 256,
50              batch_size: int = None, num_beams: int = 4) -> List[str]:
51    """Translate Marathi strings to English."""
52    single = isinstance(texts, str)
53    if single:
54        texts = [texts]
55    texts = [t if t and t.strip() else " " for t in texts]
56
57    tok, mod = models.load_translator()
58    bos = _target_lang_id(tok)
59    bs = batch_size or max(1, (config.BATCH_SIZE // 4))
60    out: List[str] = []
61
62    for i in range(0, len(texts), bs):
63        chunk = texts[i:i + bs]
64        enc = tok(chunk, padding=True, truncation=True, max_length=512,
65                  return_tensors="pt").to(config.DEVICE)
66        gen = mod.generate(**enc, forced_bos_token_id=bos,
67                           max_new_tokens=max_new_tokens, num_beams=num_beams)
68        out.extend(tok.batch_decode(gen, skip_special_tokens=True))
69
70    return out[0] if single else out
71
72
73def translate_document(text: str, max_sentences: int = 12) -> str:
74    """Sentence-split a long document, translate, and re-join."""
75    sents = sent_tokenize(text)[:max_sentences]
76    if not sents:
77        return ""
78    return " ".join(translate(sents))
79
80

83    demo = [
84        "मुख्यमंत्र्यांनी विधानसभेत नवीन शेतकरी कर्जमाफी योजनेची घोषणा केली.",
85        "भारतीय क्रिकेट संघाने दुसऱ्या कसोटी सामन्यात इंग्लंडचा पराभव केला.",
86    ]
87    for src, eng in zip(demo, translate(demo)):
88        print(f"  MR: {src}\n  EN: {eng}\n")

src/retrieve.py201 lines

(C) BM25, dense retrieval and reciprocal rank fusion.

1# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
2"""
3Information retrieval (module C).
4
5Three retrievers over the same corpus:
6
7  * BM25    -- Okapi BM25 over morphologically normalised tokens. Implemented
8               here rather than pulled from rank_bm25 so that the tokenisation
9               path (and therefore the morphology ablation) is under our
10               control and the index can be pickled with its own vocabulary.
11  * Dense   -- cosine similarity over MahaBERT-SBERT document embeddings.
12  * Hybrid  -- Reciprocal Rank Fusion of the two. RRF is used instead of a
13               weighted score sum because BM25 scores and cosine similarities
14               live on different, corpus-dependent scales.
15
16The `use_morph` flag on the BM25 index is the knob for the central experiment:
17building the same index with and without the analyser and re-running the same
18queries is what produces the retrieval numbers in the report.
19"""
20from __future__ import annotations
21
22import math
23import pickle
24import sys
25from collections import Counter, defaultdict
26from dataclasses import dataclass, field
27from pathlib import Path
28from typing import Dict, List, Optional
29
30import numpy as np
31
32sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent))
33import config                      # noqa: E402
34from src.morph import normalize_tokens  # noqa: E402
35
36K1 = 1.5
37B = 0.75
38RRF_K = 60
39
40
41@dataclass
42class Hit:
43    doc_id: int
44    score: float
45    rank: int
46    source: str = "hybrid"
47
48
49# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
50# BM25
51# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
52@dataclass
53class BM25Index:
54    use_morph: bool = True
55    postings: Dict[str, List[tuple]] = field(default_factory=lambda: defaultdict(list))
56    doc_len: List[int] = field(default_factory=list)
57    doc_ids: List[int] = field(default_factory=list)
58    avg_len: float = 0.0
59
60    def build(self, docs: List[str], doc_ids: Optional[List[int]] = None):
61        self.postings = defaultdict(list)
62        self.doc_len = []
63        self.doc_ids = doc_ids if doc_ids is not None else list(range(len(docs)))
64
65        for i, text in enumerate(docs):
66            toks = normalize_tokens(text, use_morph=self.use_morph)
67            self.doc_len.append(len(toks))
68            for term, tf in Counter(toks).items():
69                self.postings[term].append((i, tf))
70
71        self.avg_len = (sum(self.doc_len) / len(self.doc_len)) if self.doc_len else 0.0
72        self.postings = dict(self.postings)
73        return self
74
75    def search(self, query: str, top_k: int = 10) -> List[Hit]:
76        n = len(self.doc_len)
77        if n == 0:
78            return []
79        q_terms = normalize_tokens(query, use_morph=self.use_morph)
80        scores = np.zeros(n, dtype="float32")
81
82        for term in q_terms:
83            posting = self.postings.get(term)
84            if not posting:
85                continue
86            df = len(posting)
87            # BM25 idf with the +0.5 smoothing; clamped at 0 so that terms
88            # appearing in more than half the corpus cannot subtract score.
89            idf = max(math.log((n - df + 0.5) / (df + 0.5) + 1.0), 0.0)
90            for doc_i, tf in posting:
91                denom = tf + K1 * (1 - B + B * self.doc_len[doc_i] / max(self.avg_len, 1e-9))
92                scores[doc_i] += idf * (tf * (K1 + 1)) / max(denom, 1e-9)
93
94        top = np.argsort(-scores)[:top_k]
95        return [Hit(doc_id=self.doc_ids[i], score=float(scores[i]), rank=r, source="bm25")
96                for r, i in enumerate(top) if scores[i] > 0]
97
98    def save(self, path: Path):
99        Path(path).write_bytes(pickle.dumps(self))
100
101    @staticmethod
102    def load(path: Path) -> "BM25Index":
103        return pickle.loads(Path(path).read_bytes())
104
105
106# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
107# Dense
108# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
109@dataclass
110class DenseIndex:
111    vectors: np.ndarray = None
112    doc_ids: List[int] = field(default_factory=list)
113
114    def build(self, docs: List[str], doc_ids: Optional[List[int]] = None,
115              show_progress: bool = True):
116        from src import models
117        self.vectors = models.embed(docs, show_progress=show_progress)
118        self.doc_ids = doc_ids if doc_ids is not None else list(range(len(docs)))
119        return self
120
121    def search(self, query: str, top_k: int = 10) -> List[Hit]:
122        from src import models
123        if self.vectors is None or len(self.vectors) == 0:
124            return []
125        q = models.embed([query])[0]
126        sims = self.vectors @ q            # both are L2-normalised
127        top = np.argsort(-sims)[:top_k]
128        return [Hit(doc_id=self.doc_ids[i], score=float(sims[i]), rank=r, source="dense")
129                for r, i in enumerate(top)]
130
131    def save(self, path: Path):
132        np.savez_compressed(path, vectors=self.vectors,
133                            doc_ids=np.array(self.doc_ids))
134
135    @staticmethod
136    def load(path: Path) -> "DenseIndex":
137        z = np.load(path)
138        return DenseIndex(vectors=z["vectors"], doc_ids=z["doc_ids"].tolist())
139
140
141# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
142# Fusion
143# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
144def reciprocal_rank_fusion(runs: List[List[Hit]], top_k: int = 10) -> List[Hit]:
145    """Combine ranked lists by summing 1/(k + rank)."""
146    fused: Dict[int, float] = defaultdict(float)
147    for run in runs:
148        for hit in run:
149            fused[hit.doc_id] += 1.0 / (RRF_K + hit.rank + 1)
150    ordered = sorted(fused.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1])[:top_k]
151    return [Hit(doc_id=d, score=s, rank=r, source="hybrid")
152            for r, (d, s) in enumerate(ordered)]
153
154
155class HybridRetriever:
156    """BM25 + dense with RRF, with either half optional."""
157
158    def __init__(self, bm25: BM25Index = None, dense: DenseIndex = None):
159        self.bm25 = bm25
160        self.dense = dense
161
162    def search(self, query: str, top_k: int = 10,
163               mode: str = "hybrid") -> List[Hit]:
164        if mode == "bm25":
165            return self.bm25.search(query, top_k)
166        if mode == "dense":
167            return self.dense.search(query, top_k)
168        runs = []
169        if self.bm25 is not None:
170            runs.append(self.bm25.search(query, top_k * 3))
171        if self.dense is not None:
172            runs.append(self.dense.search(query, top_k * 3))
173        if not runs:
174            return []
175        return reciprocal_rank_fusion(runs, top_k)
176
177    @staticmethod
178    def load_default() -> "HybridRetriever":
179        bm25 = BM25Index.load(config.BM25_INDEX) if config.BM25_INDEX.exists() else None
180        dense = DenseIndex.load(config.DENSE_INDEX) if config.DENSE_INDEX.exists() else None
181        return HybridRetriever(bm25=bm25, dense=dense)
182
183
184if __name__ == "__main__":
185    sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8")
186    docs = [
187        "पुण्यातील शाळांमध्ये नवीन शैक्षणिक धोरण लागू करण्यात आले आहे.",
188        "भारतीय क्रिकेट संघाने कसोटी सामन्यात विजय मिळवला.",
189        "मुंबईत मेट्रो प्रकल्पाचे काम वेगाने सुरू आहे.",
190        "शाळेत विद्यार्थ्यांसाठी नवीन अभ्यासक्रम सुरू झाला.",
191    ]
192    # The query says "शाळा"; documents say "शाळांमध्ये" and "शाळेत".
193    query = "शाळा"
194    for use_morph in (False, True):
195        idx = BM25Index(use_morph=use_morph).build(docs)
196        hits = idx.search(query, top_k=3)
197        tag = "morph" if use_morph else "plain"
198        print(f"  [{tag}] query={query!r} -> {len(hits)} hits")
199        for h in hits:
200            print(f"      {h.score:.3f}  {docs[h.doc_id][:52]}")

Runs every stage over one article.

1# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
2"""
3End-to-end document pipeline.
4
5Takes one raw Marathi news article and returns a fully enriched record:
6
7    text -> morphology -> topic (D)
8                       -> entities (G)
9                       -> summary (E)
10                       -> sentiment, incl. per-entity tone (F)
11                       -> English rendering (A, optional)
12
13Retrieval (C) is not per-document -- it is built over the enriched corpus by
14scripts/build_index.py.
15
16Translation is opt-in because NLLB-600M is by far the heaviest model here and
17most batch runs do not need it.
18"""
19from __future__ import annotations
20
21import sys
22from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass, field
23from pathlib import Path
24from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional
25
26sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent))
27from src import categorize, ner, sentiment, summarize  # noqa: E402
28from src.morph import analyse, tokenize  # noqa: E402
29
30
31@dataclass
32class Document:
33    """One fully analysed news article."""
34    id: Optional[str] = None
35    title: str = ""
36    text: str = ""
37    url: str = ""
38
39    topic: str = ""
40    topic_score: float = 0.0
41    topic_scores: Dict[str, float] = field(default_factory=dict)
42
43    summary: str = ""
44    summary_sentences: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)
45
46    entities: Dict[str, List[str]] = field(default_factory=dict)
47    entity_sentiment: Dict[str, float] = field(default_factory=dict)
48
49    sentiment: str = ""
50    polarity: float = 0.0
51    sentiment_distribution: Dict[str, int] = field(default_factory=dict)
52
53    summary_en: str = ""
54    title_en: str = ""
55
56    tokens: int = 0
57    inflected_ratio: float = 0.0
58
59    def to_dict(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
60        return asdict(self)
61
62    @property
63    def search_text(self) -> str:
64        """Field actually indexed: title is repeated to weight it up."""
65        return f"{self.title} {self.title} {self.text}"
66
67
68def _morph_stats(text: str) -> tuple:
69    toks = tokenize(text)
70    if not toks:
71        return 0, 0.0
72    inflected = sum(1 for t in toks if analyse(t).is_inflected)
73    return len(toks), inflected / len(toks)
74
75
76def process(title: str, text: str, *, url: str = "", doc_id: str = None,
77            summary_k: int = 3, summary_method: str = "textrank",
78            translate: bool = False) -> Document:
79    """Run every module over a single article."""
80    doc = Document(id=doc_id, title=title or "", text=text or "", url=url)
81
82    # --- D: topic ---------------------------------------------------------
83    clf_input = f"{doc.title}. {doc.text}" if doc.title else doc.text
84    pred = categorize.classify([clf_input])[0]
85    doc.topic, doc.topic_score, doc.topic_scores = pred.label, pred.score, pred.all_scores
86
87    # --- E: summary -------------------------------------------------------
88    summ = summarize.summarize(doc.text, k=summary_k, method=summary_method)
89    doc.summary, doc.summary_sentences = summ.text, summ.sentences
90
91    # --- G: entities ------------------------------------------------------
92    # NER is run over title + summary rather than the full article: the model
93    # truncates at 256 tokens anyway, and the summary is a denser carrier of
94    # the article's principal entities than an arbitrary 256-token prefix.
95    ent_source = f"{doc.title}. {doc.summary}".strip()
96    ents = ner.extract(ent_source)
97    doc.entities = ner.summarize_entities(ents)
98
99    # --- F: sentiment -----------------------------------------------------
100    sent_doc = sentiment.analyse_document(doc.summary or doc.text)
101    doc.sentiment = sent_doc.label
102    doc.polarity = sent_doc.polarity
103    doc.sentiment_distribution = sent_doc.distribution
104    doc.entity_sentiment = sentiment.entity_sentiment(sent_doc, ents)
105
106    # --- A: translation (optional) ---------------------------------------
107    if translate:
108        from src import translate as mt
109        doc.title_en = mt.translate(doc.title) if doc.title else ""
110        doc.summary_en = mt.translate_document(doc.summary) if doc.summary else ""
111
112    # --- I: morphology statistics ----------------------------------------
113    doc.tokens, doc.inflected_ratio = _morph_stats(doc.text)
114    return doc
115
116
117def process_many(rows: List[Dict[str, str]], **kwargs) -> List[Document]:
118    """Process a list of {title, text, url, id} dicts."""
119    out = []
120    for r in rows:
121        out.append(process(r.get("title", ""), r.get("text", ""),
122                           url=r.get("url", ""), doc_id=r.get("id"), **kwargs))
123    return out
124
125
126if __name__ == "__main__":
127    import json
128    import config
129    sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8")
130
131    row = json.loads(open(config.XLSUM_TEST, encoding="utf-8").readline())
132    doc = process(row["title"], row["text"], url=row["url"], doc_id=row["id"])
133
134    print("TITLE     :", doc.title)
135    print("TOPIC     :", f"{doc.topic} ({doc.topic_score:.3f})")
136    print("SENTIMENT :", f"{doc.sentiment} ({doc.polarity:+.3f})", doc.sentiment_distribution)
137    print("TOKENS    :", doc.tokens, f"| inflected {doc.inflected_ratio:.1%}")
138    print("ENTITIES  :")
139    for k, v in doc.entities.items():
140        print(f"    {k:14s} {', '.join(v[:6])}")
141    print("SUMMARY   :", doc.summary[:300])
142    print("\nGOLD      :", row["summary"][:200])

src/ingest.py167 lines

Live news ingestion from RSS feeds.

1# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
2"""
3Live Marathi news ingestion over RSS.
4
5Lets the pipeline run on today's news instead of only the static XL-Sum
6corpus, which is what makes the dashboard demo feel real.
7
8RSS items carry only a headline and a one-line description, so `fetch_all`
9can optionally follow each link and pull the article body out of the page.
10That part is best-effort by design: every outlet has a different template, and
11a failed body fetch degrades to the RSS description rather than dropping the
12article.
13
14Only public RSS endpoints are read, one request at a time with a short delay,
15and nothing is sent anywhere.
16"""
17from __future__ import annotations
18
19import html
20import re
21import sys
22import time
23import urllib.request
24import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET
25from dataclasses import dataclass
26from pathlib import Path
27from typing import Dict, List, Optional
28
29sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent))
30
31# Verified reachable and returning Devanagari RSS.
32FEEDS: Dict[str, str] = {
33    "BBC Marathi": "https://feeds.bbci.co.uk/marathi/rss.xml",
34    "ABP Majha": "https://marathi.abplive.com/home/feed",
35    "Lokmat": "https://www.lokmat.com/rss/maharashtra.xml",
36}
37
38USER_AGENT = "Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; MarathiNewsPipeline/1.0; academic research)"
39TIMEOUT = 20
40POLITE_DELAY = 0.5
41
42_TAG_RE = re.compile(r"<[^>]+>")
43_WS_RE = re.compile(r"\s+")
44
45
46@dataclass
47class Article:
48    id: str
49    title: str
50    text: str
51    url: str
52    source: str
53    published: str = ""
54
55
56def _clean(raw: str) -> str:
57    """Strip tags and entities out of an RSS description or HTML fragment."""
58    if not raw:
59        return ""
60    txt = _TAG_RE.sub(" ", raw)
61    txt = html.unescape(txt)
62    return _WS_RE.sub(" ", txt).strip()
63
64
65def _get(url: str) -> bytes:
66    req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": USER_AGENT})
67    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=TIMEOUT) as resp:
68        return resp.read()
69
70
71def _text_of(item, *names) -> str:
72    """First non-empty child among `names`, namespace-insensitive."""
73    for name in names:
74        for child in item:
75            tag = child.tag.split("}")[-1].lower()
76            if tag == name.lower() and (child.text or "").strip():
77                return child.text.strip()
78    return ""
79
80
81def fetch_feed(name: str, url: str, limit: int = 25) -> List[Article]:
82    """Parse one RSS feed into Articles (headline + description only)."""
83    try:
84        root = ET.fromstring(_get(url))
85    except Exception as exc:                       # noqa: BLE001
86        print(f"  ! {name}: {exc}")
87        return []
88
89    out: List[Article] = []
90    # Handles both RSS <item> and Atom <entry>.
91    items = root.iter()
92    for node in items:
93        tag = node.tag.split("}")[-1].lower()
94        if tag not in ("item", "entry"):
95            continue
96        title = _clean(_text_of(node, "title"))
97        desc = _clean(_text_of(node, "description", "summary", "content"))
98        link = _text_of(node, "link", "guid")
99        pub = _text_of(node, "pubDate", "published", "updated")
100        if not title:
101            continue
102        out.append(Article(id=f"{name}:{len(out)}", title=title, text=desc,
103                           url=link, source=name, published=pub))
104        if len(out) >= limit:
105            break
106    return out
107
108
109def fetch_body(url: str) -> Optional[str]:
110    """Best-effort article body extraction. Returns None if nothing usable."""
111    try:
112        from bs4 import BeautifulSoup
113        soup = BeautifulSoup(_get(url), "html.parser")
114    except Exception:                              # noqa: BLE001
115        return None
116
117    for bad in soup(["script", "style", "nav", "header", "footer", "aside"]):
118        bad.decompose()
119
120    # Longest run of <p> text on the page is almost always the article.
121    paras = [p.get_text(" ", strip=True) for p in soup.find_all("p")]
122    paras = [p for p in paras if len(p) > 40]
123    body = " ".join(paras)
124    body = _WS_RE.sub(" ", body).strip()
125    return body if len(body) > 200 else None
126
127
128def fetch_all(limit: int = 60, with_body: bool = True,
129              feeds: Dict[str, str] = None) -> List[Dict[str, str]]:
130    """
131    Pull headlines from every feed, optionally enriching with article bodies.
132
133    Returns plain dicts shaped like the XL-Sum rows so build_corpus.py can
134    treat both sources identically.
135    """
136    feeds = feeds or FEEDS
137    per_feed = max(1, limit // max(len(feeds), 1))
138    articles: List[Article] = []
139
140    for name, url in feeds.items():
141        got = fetch_feed(name, url, limit=per_feed)
142        print(f"  {name:14s} {len(got):3d} items")
143        articles.extend(got)
144        time.sleep(POLITE_DELAY)
145
146    if with_body:
147        for a in articles:
148            if not a.url:
149                continue
150            body = fetch_body(a.url)
151            if body:
152                a.text = body
153            time.sleep(POLITE_DELAY)
154
155    return [{"id": a.id, "title": a.title, "text": a.text or a.title,
156             "url": a.url, "source": a.source, "published": a.published}
157            for a in articles]
158
159
160if __name__ == "__main__":
161    sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8")
162    rows = fetch_all(limit=9, with_body=True)
163    print(f"\nfetched {len(rows)} articles")
164    for r in rows[:5]:
165        print(f"\n  [{r['source']}] {r['title'][:70]}")
166        print(f"     {len(r['text'])} chars | {r['text'][:110]}")

src/lite.py290 lines

Small in-browser student models used by the demo page.

1# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
2"""
3Lightweight students of the MahaBERT models, small enough to run in a browser.
4
5The demo page is a single HTML file, so it cannot load the 12-class topic
6model, MahaNER or the sentiment model (each is a ~700 MB BERT). Instead it
7carries three small linear models trained by scripts/train_lite.py to
8reproduce what those models say on XL-Sum:
9
10  * topic      -- softmax regression over sublinear TF-IDF of analyser roots
11  * sentiment  -- softmax regression over words, roots and word bigrams
12  * entities   -- greedy left-to-right word tagger (a maximum-entropy Markov
13                  model) over word, root, suffix, neighbour and previous-label
14                  features
15
16How often each agrees with the model it imitates is measured on the held-out
17XL-Sum test split and shipped with the weights, so the page can say how far
18to trust it.
19
20This module is the reference implementation: the page's JavaScript is a line
21by line port of the feature functions here, and scripts/verify_demo.py checks
22that the two produce identical outputs.
23"""
24from __future__ import annotations
25
26import base64
27import json
28import math
29import re
30import sys
31from collections import Counter, defaultdict
32from pathlib import Path
33from typing import Dict, List, Tuple
34
35sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent))
36import config                                        # noqa: E402
37from src.morph import (STOPWORDS, normalize_tokens, sent_tokenize,  # noqa: E402
38                       stem, tokenize)
39
40LITE_MODELS = config.ROOT / "app" / "lite_models.json"
41
42NER_LABELS = ["O", "Person", "Location", "Organization", "Date", "Time",
43              "Measure", "Designation"]
44POLARITY = {"Negative": -1.0, "Neutral": 0.0, "Positive": 1.0}
45
46# Same boundary set as src/ner.py: a "word" for the tagger is a maximal run
47# of characters not in this set, which is exactly what MahaNER spans snap to.
48BOUNDARY = set(" \t\n\r " + "।,.;:!?\"'()[]{}<>%/\\|-–—")
49
50# How much of an article the topic student reads. The teacher truncates at
51# 256 wordpieces, so reading the whole article would teach the student to use
52# evidence the teacher never saw.
53TOPIC_MAX_TOKENS = 200
54
55
56# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
57# Features
58# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
59def topic_terms(title: str, text: str) -> List[str]:
60    joined = f"{title}. {text}" if title else text
61    return normalize_tokens(joined)[:TOPIC_MAX_TOKENS]
62
63
64def sentiment_features(sentence: str) -> List[str]:
65    toks = tokenize(sentence)
66    feats = []
67    for t in toks:
68        feats.append("w:" + t)
69        r = stem(t)
70        if r != t:
71            feats.append("r:" + r)
72    for a, b in zip(toks, toks[1:]):
73        feats.append("b:" + a + "_" + b)
74    return feats
75
76
77def words(text: str) -> List[Tuple[int, int]]:
78    """(start, end) offsets of every word, splitting on BOUNDARY characters."""
79    out, start = [], None
80    for i, ch in enumerate(text):
81        if ch in BOUNDARY:
82            if start is not None:
83                out.append((start, i))
84                start = None
85        elif start is None:
86            start = i
87    if start is not None:
88        out.append((start, len(text)))
89    return out
90
91
92_DIGITS_RE = re.compile(r"[0-9\u0966-\u096F]+")
93_ASCII_RE = re.compile(r"[\x00-\x7F]+")
94
95
96def _shape(w: str) -> str:
97    # Explicit character classes rather than str.isdigit()/isascii(), whose
98    # Unicode rules differ from JavaScript's and would break parity.
99    if _DIGITS_RE.fullmatch(w):
100        return "digit"
101    if _ASCII_RE.fullmatch(w):
102        return "latin"
103    return "deva"
104
105
106def ner_features(toks: List[str], i: int, prev: str, prev2: str) -> List[str]:
107    """Features for word i; prev/prev2 are the labels already assigned."""
108    w = toks[i]
109    r = stem(w)
110    p = toks[i - 1] if i > 0 else "<s>"
111    n = toks[i + 1] if i + 1 < len(toks) else "</s>"
112    n2 = toks[i + 2] if i + 2 < len(toks) else "</s>"
113    feats = [
114        "bias", "w:" + w, "r:" + r, "s1:" + w[-1:], "s2:" + w[-2:], "s3:" + w[-3:],
115        "p3:" + w[:3], "sh:" + _shape(w), "sw:" + str(w in STOPWORDS),
116        "pw:" + p, "pr:" + stem(p), "nw:" + n, "nr:" + stem(n), "nw2:" + n2,
117        "pl:" + prev, "pl2:" + prev + "|" + prev2, "plw:" + prev + "|" + r,
118        "pwn:" + p + "|" + w, "wn:" + w + "|" + n,
119    ]
120    if i == 0:
121        feats.append("first")
122    return feats
123
124
125# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
126# Inference
127# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
128def _softmax(z: List[float]) -> List[float]:
129    m = max(z)
130    e = [math.exp(v - m) for v in z]
131    s = sum(e)
132    return [v / s for v in e]
133
134
135def unpack(b64: str, cols: int) -> List[List[int]]:
136    """Rows of int8 weights from the base64 blob written by train_lite.py."""
137    raw = base64.b64decode(b64)
138    vals = [v - 256 if v > 127 else v for v in raw]
139    return [vals[i:i + cols] for i in range(0, len(vals), cols)]
140
141
142class Lite:
143    """Loaded student models. Weights are int8 values times one scale."""
144
145    def __init__(self, data: dict):
146        self.data = data
147        t = data["topic"]
148        self.topic_labels = t["labels"]
149        self.topic_idf = dict(zip(t["terms"], t["idf"]))
150        self.topic_w = dict(zip(t["terms"], unpack(t["W"], len(t["labels"]))))
151        self.topic_b = t["b"]
152        self.topic_scale = t["scale"]
153
154        s = data["sentiment"]
155        self.sent_labels = s["labels"]
156        self.sent_w = dict(zip(s["feats"], unpack(s["W"], len(s["labels"]))))
157        self.sent_b = s["b"]
158        self.sent_scale = s["scale"]
159
160        n = data["ner"]
161        self.ner_labels = n["labels"]
162        self.ner_w = dict(zip(n["feats"], unpack(n["W"], len(n["labels"]))))
163        self.ner_b = n["b"]
164        self.ner_scale = n["scale"]
165
166    @classmethod
167    def load(cls, path: Path = LITE_MODELS) -> "Lite":
168        return cls(json.loads(Path(path).read_text(encoding="utf-8")))
169
170    # ---- topic ----------------------------------------------------------
171    def topic(self, title: str, text: str) -> Dict[str, float]:
172        tf = Counter(t for t in topic_terms(title, text) if t in self.topic_w)
173        vec = {t: (1 + math.log(c)) * self.topic_idf[t] for t, c in tf.items()}
174        norm = math.sqrt(sum(v * v for v in vec.values())) or 1.0
175        k = len(self.topic_labels)
176        z = [0.0] * k
177        for t, v in vec.items():
178            row = self.topic_w[t]
179            for j in range(k):
180                z[j] += row[j] * v / norm
181        z = [z[j] * self.topic_scale + self.topic_b[j] for j in range(k)]
182        return dict(zip(self.topic_labels, _softmax(z)))
183
184    # ---- sentiment ------------------------------------------------------
185    def sentence_sentiment(self, sentence: str) -> Dict[str, float]:
186        feats = [f for f in set(sentiment_features(sentence)) if f in self.sent_w]
187        k = len(self.sent_labels)
188        z = [0.0] * k
189        inv = 1.0 / math.sqrt(len(feats)) if feats else 0.0
190        for f in sorted(feats):
191            row = self.sent_w[f]
192            for j in range(k):
193                z[j] += row[j] * inv
194        z = [z[j] * self.sent_scale + self.sent_b[j] for j in range(k)]
195        return dict(zip(self.sent_labels, _softmax(z)))
196
197    def document_sentiment(self, text: str) -> dict:
198        """Same aggregation as src/sentiment.analyse_document."""
199        sents = sent_tokenize(text)
200        if not sents:
201            return {"label": "Neutral", "polarity": 0.0,
202                    "distribution": {"Negative": 0, "Neutral": 0, "Positive": 0},
203                    "sentences": []}
204        scored = []
205        for s in sents:
206            p = self.sentence_sentiment(s)
207            label = max(p, key=p.get)
208            pol = sum(POLARITY[k] * v for k, v in p.items())
209            scored.append({"text": s, "label": label, "polarity": pol})
210        weights = [max(len(s["text"]), 1) for s in scored]
211        pol = sum(s["polarity"] * w for s, w in zip(scored, weights)) / sum(weights)
212        label = "Positive" if pol > 0.15 else "Negative" if pol < -0.15 else "Neutral"
213        dist = {"Negative": 0, "Neutral": 0, "Positive": 0}
214        for s in scored:
215            dist[s["label"]] += 1
216        return {"label": label, "polarity": pol, "distribution": dist,
217                "sentences": scored}
218
219    # ---- entities -------------------------------------------------------
220    def tag(self, text: str) -> List[Tuple[int, int, str]]:
221        """Word-level labels, as (start, end, label) for every word."""
222        offs = words(text)
223        toks = [text[s:e] for s, e in offs]
224        k = len(self.ner_labels)
225        out, prev, prev2 = [], "O", "O"
226        for i in range(len(toks)):
227            z = list(self.ner_b)
228            for f in ner_features(toks, i, prev, prev2):
229                row = self.ner_w.get(f)
230                if row is not None:
231                    for j in range(k):
232                        z[j] += row[j] * self.ner_scale
233            best = max(range(k), key=lambda j: z[j])
234            lab = self.ner_labels[best]
235            out.append((offs[i][0], offs[i][1], lab))
236            prev2, prev = prev, lab
237        return out
238
239    def entities(self, text: str) -> List[Tuple[int, int, str]]:
240        """Merge adjacent same-label words separated by one character."""
241        spans: List[list] = []
242        for s, e, lab in self.tag(text):
243            if lab == "O":
244                continue
245            if spans and spans[-1][2] == lab and s - spans[-1][1] <= 1:
246                spans[-1][1] = e
247            else:
248                spans.append([s, e, lab])
249        return [tuple(x) for x in spans]
250
251
252def group_entities(text: str, spans) -> Dict[str, List[str]]:
253    """Same grouping as src/ner.summarize_entities: root key, surface label."""
254    counts: Counter = Counter()
255    surfaces: Dict[tuple, Counter] = defaultdict(Counter)
256    for s, e, lab in spans:
257        surf = text[s:e].strip()
258        if not surf:
259            continue
260        parts = surf.split()
261        canon = " ".join(parts[:-1] + [stem(parts[-1])])
262        counts[(lab, canon)] += 1
263        surfaces[(lab, canon)][surf] += 1
264    out: Dict[str, List[str]] = defaultdict(list)
265    for (lab, canon), _ in counts.most_common():
266        out[lab].append(surfaces[(lab, canon)].most_common(1)[0][0])
267    return dict(out)
268
269
270def analyse(model: "Lite", title: str, text: str) -> dict:
271    """
272    The whole in-browser pipeline, mirroring src/pipeline.process with the
273    students in place of the MahaBERT models. The page's JavaScript pipeline()
274    must return the same thing; scripts/verify_demo.py checks that it does.
275    """
276    from src.summarize import summarize
277    title, text = (title or "").strip(), (text or "").strip()
278    summ = summarize(text, k=3)
279    summary = summ.text
280    ent_source = f"{title}. {summary}".strip()
281    sent = model.document_sentiment(summary or text)
282    return {
283        "topic_scores": model.topic(title, text),
284        "summary": summary,
285        "entities": group_entities(ent_source, model.entities(ent_source)),
286        "sentiment": sent["label"],
287        "polarity": sent["polarity"],
288        "sentiment_distribution": sent["distribution"],
289    }
