Downloads the XL-Sum and MahaNews datasets.

1# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
2"""
3Fetch the two public corpora this project is built on.
4
5    python scripts/download_data.py
6
7  * XL-Sum (Marathi) -- 10,903 / 1,362 / 1,362 BBC Marathi articles with
8    human-written abstractive summaries. Used as the document corpus and as
9    the gold standard for the summarisation evaluation.
10    https://huggingface.co/datasets/csebuetnlp/xlsum
11
12  * MahaNews (headline split, via MTEB) -- 9,673 / 2,048 Marathi headlines
13    labelled entertainment / sports / state. Used to fine-tune the topic
14    classifier and to score it.
15    https://huggingface.co/datasets/mteb/MarathiNewsClassification
16
17Both are downloaded straight over HTTPS rather than through `datasets`, which
18keeps the dependency list short and means no Hub authentication is needed.
19Nothing here is uploaded; the requests are read-only downloads.
20"""
21from __future__ import annotations
22
23import sys
24import tarfile
25import urllib.request
26from pathlib import Path
27
28sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent))
29sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8")
30
31import config  # noqa: E402
32
33XLSUM_URL = ("https://huggingface.co/datasets/csebuetnlp/xlsum/resolve/main/"
34             "data/marathi_XLSum_v2.0.tar.bz2")
35MAHANEWS = {
36    "mahanews_train.parquet": ("https://huggingface.co/datasets/mteb/"
37                               "MarathiNewsClassification/resolve/main/"
38                               "data/train-00000-of-00001.parquet"),
39    "mahanews_test.parquet": ("https://huggingface.co/datasets/mteb/"
40                              "MarathiNewsClassification/resolve/main/"
41                              "data/test-00000-of-00001.parquet"),
42}
43
44
45def fetch(url: str, dest: Path):
46    if dest.exists() and dest.stat().st_size > 0:
47        print(f"  = {dest.name} (already present, {dest.stat().st_size:,} bytes)")
48        return
49    print(f"  > {dest.name} ...", end="", flush=True)
50    urllib.request.urlretrieve(url, dest)
51    print(f" {dest.stat().st_size:,} bytes")
52
53

1# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
2"""
3Enrich raw articles into the analysed corpus that the index and dashboard use.
4
5Runs the whole pipeline over XL-Sum Marathi (or a live RSS pull) and writes one
6JSON object per line to data/processed/corpus.jsonl.
7
8The stages are deliberately run *stage-by-stage over the whole batch* rather
9than document-by-document: the GPU is only worth using when it gets a full
10batch, and this way each model is resident once instead of being swapped in
11and out per article.
12
13    python scripts/build_corpus.py --limit 1500
14    python scripts/build_corpus.py --source rss --translate
15"""
16from __future__ import annotations
17
18import argparse
19import json
20import sys
21import time
22from pathlib import Path
23
24sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent))
25sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8")
26
27import config                                    # noqa: E402
28from src import categorize, ner, sentiment, summarize  # noqa: E402
29from src.morph import analyse, tokenize          # noqa: E402
30from src.pipeline import Document                # noqa: E402
31
32
33def load_xlsum(limit: int, split: str = "train"):
34    path = {"train": config.XLSUM_TRAIN, "val": config.XLSUM_VAL,
35            "test": config.XLSUM_TEST}[split]
36    rows = []
37    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
38        for line in fh:
39            if limit and len(rows) >= limit:
40                break
41            r = json.loads(line)
42            if len(r.get("text", "")) < 200:      # skip stubs
43                continue
44            rows.append({"id": r["id"], "title": r["title"], "text": r["text"],
45                         "url": r.get("url", ""), "gold_summary": r.get("summary", "")})
46    return rows
47
48
49def load_rss(limit: int):
50    from src.ingest import fetch_all
51    return fetch_all(limit=limit)
52
53
54def morph_stats(text: str):
55    toks = tokenize(text)
56    if not toks:
57        return 0, 0.0
58    return len(toks), sum(1 for t in toks if analyse(t).is_inflected) / len(toks)
59
60
61def main():
62    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
63    ap.add_argument("--limit", type=int, default=1500)
64    ap.add_argument("--source", choices=["xlsum", "rss"], default="xlsum")
65    ap.add_argument("--split", default="train")
66    ap.add_argument("--summary-k", type=int, default=3)
67    ap.add_argument("--method", default="textrank")
68    ap.add_argument("--translate", action="store_true",
69                    help="also render English title/summary (slow: NLLB-600M)")
70    ap.add_argument("--out", default=str(config.CORPUS_JSONL))
71    args = ap.parse_args()
72
73    t0 = time.time()
74    rows = load_rss(args.limit) if args.source == "rss" else load_xlsum(args.limit, args.split)
75    print(f"[1/6] loaded {len(rows)} articles from {args.source}")
76
77    docs = [Document(id=str(r.get("id") or i), title=r.get("title", ""),
78                     text=r.get("text", ""), url=r.get("url", ""))
79            for i, r in enumerate(rows)]
80
81    # --- E: summaries (CPU, no model) ------------------------------------
82    for d in docs:
83        s = summarize.summarize(d.text, k=args.summary_k, method=args.method)
84        d.summary, d.summary_sentences = s.text, s.sentences
85    print(f"[2/6] summarised            ({time.time() - t0:.0f}s)")
86
87    # --- D: topic, batched ------------------------------------------------
88    preds = categorize.classify([f"{d.title}. {d.text}" for d in docs])
89    for d, p in zip(docs, preds):
90        d.topic, d.topic_score, d.topic_scores = p.label, p.score, p.all_scores
91    print(f"[3/6] categorised           ({time.time() - t0:.0f}s)")
92
93    # --- G + F: entities and sentiment ------------------------------------
94    for n, d in enumerate(docs, 1):
95        ents = ner.extract(f"{d.title}. {d.summary}".strip())
96        d.entities = ner.summarize_entities(ents)
97        sd = sentiment.analyse_document(d.summary or d.text)
98        d.sentiment, d.polarity = sd.label, sd.polarity
99        d.sentiment_distribution = sd.distribution
100        d.entity_sentiment = sentiment.entity_sentiment(sd, ents)
101        if n % 250 == 0:
102            print(f"      ...{n}/{len(docs)}  ({time.time() - t0:.0f}s)", flush=True)
103    print(f"[4/6] entities + sentiment  ({time.time() - t0:.0f}s)")
104
105    # --- A: translation (optional) ---------------------------------------
106    if args.translate:
107        from src import translate as mt
108        titles = mt.translate([d.title for d in docs])
109        summaries = mt.translate([d.summary[:900] for d in docs])
110        for d, t, s in zip(docs, titles, summaries):
111            d.title_en, d.summary_en = t, s
112        print(f"[5/6] translated            ({time.time() - t0:.0f}s)")
113    else:
114        print("[5/6] translation skipped (pass --translate to enable)")
115
116    # --- I: morphology stats ---------------------------------------------
117    for d in docs:
118        d.tokens, d.inflected_ratio = morph_stats(d.text)
119
120    out = Path(args.out)
121    with open(out, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
122        for d, r in zip(docs, rows):
123            rec = d.to_dict()
124            if r.get("gold_summary"):
125                rec["gold_summary"] = r["gold_summary"]
126            fh.write(json.dumps(rec, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
127
128    avg_infl = sum(d.inflected_ratio for d in docs) / max(len(docs), 1)
129    print(f"[6/6] wrote {len(docs)} docs -> {out}")
130    print(f"      mean inflected-token ratio: {avg_infl:.1%}")
131    print(f"      total {time.time() - t0:.0f}s")
132
133
134if __name__ == "__main__":
135    main()

1# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
2"""
3Build the retrieval indexes over the enriched corpus.
4
5    python scripts/build_index.py                # BM25 (morph) + dense
6    python scripts/build_index.py --no-dense     # BM25 only, no GPU needed
7    python scripts/build_index.py --plain-bm25   # ablation index, no morphology
8
9The `--plain-bm25` variant writes a second index built from raw whitespace
10tokens. Keeping both on disk is what lets scripts/evaluate.py run the
11morphology ablation without rebuilding anything.
12"""
13from __future__ import annotations
14
15import argparse
16import json
17import sys
18import time
19from pathlib import Path
20
21sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent))
22sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8")
23
24import config                                     # noqa: E402
25from src.retrieve import BM25Index, DenseIndex    # noqa: E402
26
27PLAIN_BM25_INDEX = config.INDEX / "bm25_plain.pkl"
28
29
30def load_corpus(path: Path):
31    if not path.exists():
32        sys.exit(f"corpus not found: {path}\nRun scripts/build_corpus.py first.")
33    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
34        return [json.loads(line) for line in fh]
35
36
37def search_text(rec: dict) -> str:
38    """Title is repeated so it outweighs the body in BM25 term frequency."""
39    return f"{rec.get('title', '')} {rec.get('title', '')} {rec.get('text', '')}"
40
41
42def main():
43    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
44    ap.add_argument("--corpus", default=str(config.CORPUS_JSONL))
45    ap.add_argument("--no-dense", action="store_true")
46    ap.add_argument("--plain-bm25", action="store_true",
47                    help="also build a morphology-free index for the ablation")
48    args = ap.parse_args()
49
50    corpus = load_corpus(Path(args.corpus))
51    texts = [search_text(r) for r in corpus]
52    doc_ids = list(range(len(corpus)))
53    print(f"indexing {len(corpus)} documents")
54
55    t0 = time.time()
56    bm25 = BM25Index(use_morph=True).build(texts, doc_ids)
57    bm25.save(config.BM25_INDEX)
58    print(f"  BM25 (morph) : {len(bm25.postings):>7,} terms  "
59          f"avg_len={bm25.avg_len:.0f}  ({time.time() - t0:.1f}s)")
60
61    if args.plain_bm25:
62        t1 = time.time()
63        plain = BM25Index(use_morph=False).build(texts, doc_ids)
64        plain.save(PLAIN_BM25_INDEX)
65        print(f"  BM25 (plain) : {len(plain.postings):>7,} terms  "
66              f"({time.time() - t1:.1f}s)")
67        shrink = 1 - len(bm25.postings) / max(len(plain.postings), 1)
68        print(f"  vocabulary reduced by {shrink:.1%} through morphological normalisation")
69
70    if not args.no_dense:
71        t2 = time.time()
72        # Embed title + summary rather than the full article: the encoder
73        # truncates at 256 tokens, and the summary is a better 256 tokens than
74        # an arbitrary prefix of the body.
75        dense_texts = [f"{r.get('title', '')}. {r.get('summary', '')}" for r in corpus]
76        dense = DenseIndex().build(dense_texts, doc_ids)
77        dense.save(config.DENSE_INDEX)
78        print(f"  Dense        : {dense.vectors.shape}  ({time.time() - t2:.1f}s)")
79
80    print(f"done in {time.time() - t0:.1f}s -> {config.INDEX}")
81
82
83if __name__ == "__main__":
84    main()

scripts/train_classifier.py167 lines

Fine-tunes MahaBERT as a topic classifier.

1# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
2"""
3Fine-tune MahaBERT for Marathi news topic classification.
4
5Trains `l3cube-pune/marathi-bert-v2` on the MahaNews headline split
6(entertainment / sports / state) and writes the result to models/topic-clf,
7which src/categorize.py then picks up automatically.
8
9    python scripts/train_classifier.py --epochs 3
10
11Written as a plain PyTorch loop rather than transformers.Trainer: it avoids
12the `accelerate` dependency, keeps the mixed-precision and gradient-clipping
13behaviour explicit, and is small enough to read. Mixed precision plus a batch
14size of 16 keeps a 110M-parameter BERT inside 4 GB of VRAM.
15"""
16from __future__ import annotations
17
18import argparse
19import json
20import sys
21import time
22from pathlib import Path
23
24import numpy as np
25import torch
26from torch.utils.data import DataLoader, Dataset
27
28sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent))
29sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8")
30
31import config  # noqa: E402
32
33LABELS = ["entertainment", "sports", "state"]
34LABEL2ID = {l: i for i, l in enumerate(LABELS)}
35
36
37class NewsDataset(Dataset):
38    def __init__(self, texts, labels, tokenizer, max_len=128):
39        self.texts, self.labels = texts, labels
40        self.tok, self.max_len = tokenizer, max_len
41
42    def __len__(self):
43        return len(self.texts)
44
45    def __getitem__(self, i):
46        enc = self.tok(self.texts[i], truncation=True, max_length=self.max_len,
47                       padding="max_length", return_tensors="pt")
48        item = {k: v.squeeze(0) for k, v in enc.items()}
49        item["labels"] = torch.tensor(self.labels[i], dtype=torch.long)
50        return item
51
52
53def load_split(path: Path):
54    import pandas as pd
55    df = pd.read_parquet(path)
56    # The parquet ships integer labels; config.MAHANEWS_LABELS maps them to
57    # the names used everywhere else in the project.
58    texts = df["text"].astype(str).tolist()
59    labels = [LABEL2ID[config.MAHANEWS_LABELS[int(x)]] for x in df["label"]]
60    return texts, labels
61
62
63@torch.no_grad()
64def evaluate(model, loader, device):
65    model.eval()
66    preds, golds = [], []
67    for batch in loader:
68        labels = batch.pop("labels")
69        batch = {k: v.to(device) for k, v in batch.items()}
70        with torch.autocast(device_type=device, dtype=torch.float16,
71                            enabled=(device == "cuda")):
72            logits = model(**batch).logits
73        preds.extend(logits.float().argmax(-1).cpu().tolist())
74        golds.extend(labels.tolist())
75    return np.array(preds), np.array(golds)
76
77
78def report(preds, golds):
79    from sklearn.metrics import classification_report, confusion_matrix
80    acc = float((preds == golds).mean())
81    rep = classification_report(golds, preds, target_names=LABELS,
82                                digits=4, zero_division=0, output_dict=True)
83    print(classification_report(golds, preds, target_names=LABELS,
84                                digits=4, zero_division=0))
85    print("confusion matrix (rows = gold):")
86    print(confusion_matrix(golds, preds))
87    return acc, rep
88
89
90def main():
91    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
92    ap.add_argument("--epochs", type=int, default=3)
93    ap.add_argument("--batch-size", type=int, default=16)
94    ap.add_argument("--lr", type=float, default=2e-5)
95    ap.add_argument("--max-len", type=int, default=128)
96    ap.add_argument("--limit", type=int, default=0, help="subsample for a quick run")
97    ap.add_argument("--out", default=str(config.CUSTOM_TOPIC_DIR))
98    args = ap.parse_args()
99
100    from transformers import AutoModelForSequenceClassification, AutoTokenizer
101
102    device = config.DEVICE
103    tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(config.MODEL_BASE_BERT)
104    model = AutoModelForSequenceClassification.from_pretrained(
105        config.MODEL_BASE_BERT, num_labels=len(LABELS),
106        id2label={i: l for i, l in enumerate(LABELS)}, label2id=LABEL2ID,
107    ).to(device)
108
109    tr_x, tr_y = load_split(config.MAHANEWS_TRAIN)
110    te_x, te_y = load_split(config.MAHANEWS_TEST)
111    if args.limit:
112        tr_x, tr_y = tr_x[:args.limit], tr_y[:args.limit]
113    print(f"train={len(tr_x)}  test={len(te_x)}  device={device}")
114
115    train_dl = DataLoader(NewsDataset(tr_x, tr_y, tok, args.max_len),
116                          batch_size=args.batch_size, shuffle=True)
117    test_dl = DataLoader(NewsDataset(te_x, te_y, tok, args.max_len),
118                         batch_size=args.batch_size)
119
120    opt = torch.optim.AdamW(model.parameters(), lr=args.lr, weight_decay=0.01)
121    steps = len(train_dl) * args.epochs
122    sched = torch.optim.lr_scheduler.OneCycleLR(
123        opt, max_lr=args.lr, total_steps=steps, pct_start=0.1, anneal_strategy="linear")
124    scaler = torch.amp.GradScaler(device, enabled=(device == "cuda"))
125
126    t0 = time.time()
127    for epoch in range(1, args.epochs + 1):
128        model.train()
129        running = 0.0
130        for step, batch in enumerate(train_dl, 1):
131            batch = {k: v.to(device) for k, v in batch.items()}
132            opt.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
133            with torch.autocast(device_type=device, dtype=torch.float16,
134                                enabled=(device == "cuda")):
135                loss = model(**batch).loss
136            scaler.scale(loss).backward()
137            scaler.unscale_(opt)
138            torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(model.parameters(), 1.0)
139            scaler.step(opt)
140            scaler.update()
141            sched.step()
142            running += loss.item()
143            if step % 100 == 0:
144                print(f"  epoch {epoch} step {step}/{len(train_dl)} "
145                      f"loss={running / step:.4f} ({time.time() - t0:.0f}s)", flush=True)
146
147        preds, golds = evaluate(model, test_dl, device)
148        print(f"\nepoch {epoch}: test accuracy = {(preds == golds).mean():.4f}\n")
149
150    print("=" * 60)
151    acc, rep = report(*evaluate(model, test_dl, device))
152
153    out = Path(args.out)
154    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
155    model.save_pretrained(out)
156    tok.save_pretrained(out)
157    (out / "metrics.json").write_text(
158        json.dumps({"accuracy": acc, "report": rep,
159                    "epochs": args.epochs, "lr": args.lr,
160                    "base_model": config.MODEL_BASE_BERT}, indent=2),
161        encoding="utf-8")
162    print(f"\nsaved -> {out}  (accuracy {acc:.4f}, {time.time() - t0:.0f}s)")
163
164
165if __name__ == "__main__":
166    main()

scripts/evaluate.py486 lines

All experiments, plus a Marathi-aware ROUGE implementation.

1# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
2"""
3Evaluation suite. Five experiments, each runnable on its own:
4
5    python scripts/evaluate.py --task retrieval       # full-headline queries
6    python scripts/evaluate.py --task shortquery      # 1-3 word queries
7    python scripts/evaluate.py --task crossinfl       # when morphology decides
8    python scripts/evaluate.py --task summarization
9    python scripts/evaluate.py --task classification
10    python scripts/evaluate.py --task all
11
12RETRIEVAL (1, 1b, 1c) is what the project is built around: the same BM25 index
13is constructed with and without the morphological analyser and queried the
14same way. The three variants exist because the first one alone is misleading.
15
16  1  full-headline queries     -- morphology gives a small gain (+3.9% MRR)
17  1b short, realistic queries  -- morphology gives no gain, and at 1-2 terms
18                                  is slightly worse
19  1c the subset where a query term occurs in the body only in a different
20     inflection -- 68% of articles have one, and there the plain index returns
21     an empty result page 14.4% of the time against 1.1% with morphology
22
23Taken together: morphology is recall insurance for Marathi search, not a
24ranking improvement. Reporting only experiment 1 would overstate it, and
25reporting only the hand-picked शाळा example would overstate it badly.
26
27SUMMARIZATION scores extractive summaries against XL-Sum's gold abstracts with
28ROUGE-1/2/L. ROUGE is implemented here rather than taken from `rouge_score`,
29whose default tokenizer strips non-ASCII and would score every Marathi summary
30as 0. Scores are reported over both raw and morphologically normalised tokens:
31the raw numbers are comparable with published work, the normalised ones are
32the fairer measurement for a language where the same lemma surfaces in half a
33dozen forms.
34
35Note on the ceiling: XL-Sum summaries are abstractive and roughly one
36sentence, so an extractive system cannot reach a high ROUGE here. The lead
37baseline is included so the comparison is against something honest.
38"""
39from __future__ import annotations
40
41import argparse
42import json
43import random
44import sys
45import time
46from collections import Counter
47from pathlib import Path
48from typing import List
49
50import numpy as np
51
52sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent))
53sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8")
54
55import config                                        # noqa: E402
56from src.morph import normalize_tokens, tokenize     # noqa: E402
57
58SEED = 13
59
60
61# ==========================================================================
62# ROUGE
63# ==========================================================================
64def _f1(match: int, pred_n: int, gold_n: int) -> float:
65    if match == 0 or pred_n == 0 or gold_n == 0:
66        return 0.0
67    p, r = match / pred_n, match / gold_n
68    return 2 * p * r / (p + r)
69
70
71def _ngrams(tokens: List[str], n: int) -> Counter:
72    return Counter(tuple(tokens[i:i + n]) for i in range(len(tokens) - n + 1))
73
74
75def rouge_n(pred: List[str], gold: List[str], n: int) -> float:
76    p, g = _ngrams(pred, n), _ngrams(gold, n)
77    overlap = sum((p & g).values())
78    return _f1(overlap, max(sum(p.values()), 0), max(sum(g.values()), 0))
79
80
81def rouge_l(pred: List[str], gold: List[str]) -> float:
82    """F1 over the longest common subsequence (O(n*m), quadratic memory-free)."""
83    if not pred or not gold:
84        return 0.0
85    prev = [0] * (len(gold) + 1)
86    for a in pred:
87        cur = [0]
88        for j, b in enumerate(gold):
89            cur.append(prev[j] + 1 if a == b else max(cur[j], prev[j + 1]))
90        prev = cur
91    return _f1(prev[-1], len(pred), len(gold))
92
93
94def rouge_all(pred_text: str, gold_text: str, use_morph: bool) -> dict:
95    if use_morph:
96        p = normalize_tokens(pred_text, drop_stopwords=False)
97        g = normalize_tokens(gold_text, drop_stopwords=False)
98    else:
99        p, g = tokenize(pred_text), tokenize(gold_text)
100    return {"rouge1": rouge_n(p, g, 1), "rouge2": rouge_n(p, g, 2),
101            "rougeL": rouge_l(p, g)}
102
103
104# ==========================================================================
105# Experiment 1 -- retrieval
106# ==========================================================================
107def eval_retrieval(corpus, n_queries=300, top_k=10, include_dense=True):
108    """
109    Known-item retrieval: each query is one document's title, and the correct
110    answer is that document. Titles are held out of the indexed text so the
111    task is not trivially solved by an exact string match.
112    """
113    from src.retrieve import BM25Index, DenseIndex, HybridRetriever
114
115    random.seed(SEED)
116    bodies = [r.get("text", "") for r in corpus]
117    doc_ids = list(range(len(corpus)))
118
119    eligible = [i for i, r in enumerate(corpus)
120                if len(r.get("title", "").split()) >= 4 and len(r.get("text", "")) > 300]
121    queries = random.sample(eligible, min(n_queries, len(eligible)))
122    print(f"  {len(corpus)} docs indexed, {len(queries)} known-item queries\n")
123
124    runs = {}
125    built = {}
126
127    for use_morph in (False, True):
128        tag = "BM25 + morphology" if use_morph else "BM25 (plain tokens)"
129        t0 = time.time()
130        idx = BM25Index(use_morph=use_morph).build(bodies, doc_ids)
131        built[use_morph] = idx
132        results = []
133        for qi in queries:
134            hits = idx.search(corpus[qi]["title"], top_k=top_k)
135            rank = next((h.rank for h in hits if h.doc_id == qi), None)
136            results.append(rank)
137        runs[tag] = results
138        runs[tag + "::vocab"] = len(idx.postings)
139        runs[tag + "::time"] = time.time() - t0
140
141    if include_dense:
142        t0 = time.time()
143        dense_texts = [f"{r.get('summary', '') or r.get('text', '')[:600]}" for r in corpus]
144        dense = DenseIndex().build(dense_texts, doc_ids, show_progress=False)
145        results = []
146        for qi in queries:
147            hits = dense.search(corpus[qi]["title"], top_k=top_k)
148            rank = next((h.rank for h in hits if h.doc_id == qi), None)
149            results.append(rank)
150        runs["Dense (MahaBERT-SBERT)"] = results
151        runs["Dense (MahaBERT-SBERT)::time"] = time.time() - t0
152
153        hybrid = HybridRetriever(bm25=built[True], dense=dense)
154        results = []
155        for qi in queries:
156            hits = hybrid.search(corpus[qi]["title"], top_k=top_k)
157            rank = next((h.rank for h in hits if h.doc_id == qi), None)
158            results.append(rank)
159        runs["Hybrid (RRF)"] = results
160
161    # ---- report ----
162    header = f"  {'system':26s} {'R@1':>7s} {'R@5':>7s} {'R@10':>7s} {'MRR@10':>8s}"
163    print(header)
164    print("  " + "-" * (len(header) - 2))
165    table = {}
166    for name, ranks in runs.items():
167        if "::" in name:
168            continue
169        found = [r for r in ranks if r is not None]
170        r1 = sum(1 for r in found if r < 1) / len(ranks)
171        r5 = sum(1 for r in found if r < 5) / len(ranks)
172        r10 = len(found) / len(ranks)
173        mrr = sum(1 / (r + 1) for r in found) / len(ranks)
174        table[name] = {"R@1": r1, "R@5": r5, "R@10": r10, "MRR@10": mrr}
175        print(f"  {name:26s} {r1:7.3f} {r5:7.3f} {r10:7.3f} {mrr:8.3f}")
176
177    plain = table.get("BM25 (plain tokens)", {}).get("MRR@10", 0)
178    morph = table.get("BM25 + morphology", {}).get("MRR@10", 0)
179    if plain:
180        print(f"\n  morphology lifts BM25 MRR@10 by {(morph - plain) / plain:+.1%}")
181    v_plain = runs.get("BM25 (plain tokens)::vocab", 0)
182    v_morph = runs.get("BM25 + morphology::vocab", 0)
183    if v_plain:
184        print(f"  vocabulary: {v_plain:,} -> {v_morph:,} types "
185              f"({1 - v_morph / v_plain:.1%} smaller)")
186    return table
187
188
189def eval_short_queries(corpus, n_queries=300, top_k=10, lengths=(1, 2, 3)):
190    """
191    The same known-item task, but with realistically short queries.
192
193    A full headline contains eight or ten content words, so even if the
194    analyser rescues two of them the other six already found the document --
195    which is why the full-title experiment understates what morphology does.
196    Real search traffic is one to three words, where a single unmatched term
197    is the difference between a hit and an empty result page.
198
199    Query terms are taken verbatim from the document's *title* and matched
200    against its *body*. Nothing is lemmatised on the way in: the two fields
201    simply inflect the same nouns differently, which is the effect being
202    measured. Taking roots as queries would bias the test toward the analyser.
203    """
204    from src.retrieve import BM25Index
205    from src.morph import STOPWORDS
206
207    random.seed(SEED)
208    bodies = [r.get("text", "") for r in corpus]
209    doc_ids = list(range(len(corpus)))
210
211    def content_words(title):
212        return [t for t in tokenize(title) if t not in STOPWORDS and len(t) > 2]
213
214    eligible = [i for i, r in enumerate(corpus)
215                if len(content_words(r.get("title", ""))) >= max(lengths)
216                and len(r.get("text", "")) > 300]
217    sample = random.sample(eligible, min(n_queries, len(eligible)))
218
219    indexes = {m: BM25Index(use_morph=m).build(bodies, doc_ids) for m in (False, True)}
220
221    print(f"  {len(sample)} queries, terms taken verbatim from each article's title\n")
222    print(f"  {'query len':>10s} {'plain MRR':>11s} {'morph MRR':>11s} "
223          f"{'plain R@10':>11s} {'morph R@10':>11s} {'zero-hit plain':>15s}")
224    print("  " + "-" * 74)
225
226    table = {}
227    for n in lengths:
228        stats = {}
229        for use_morph, idx in indexes.items():
230            ranks, empty = [], 0
231            for qi in sample:
232                q = " ".join(content_words(corpus[qi]["title"])[:n])
233                hits = idx.search(q, top_k=top_k)
234                if not hits:
235                    empty += 1
236                ranks.append(next((h.rank for h in hits if h.doc_id == qi), None))
237            found = [r for r in ranks if r is not None]
238            stats[use_morph] = {
239                "MRR@10": sum(1 / (r + 1) for r in found) / len(ranks),
240                "R@10": len(found) / len(ranks),
241                "zero_hit_rate": empty / len(ranks),
242            }
243        table[n] = {"plain": stats[False], "morph": stats[True]}
244        print(f"  {n:>10d} {stats[False]['MRR@10']:>11.3f} {stats[True]['MRR@10']:>11.3f} "
245              f"{stats[False]['R@10']:>11.3f} {stats[True]['R@10']:>11.3f} "
246              f"{stats[False]['zero_hit_rate']:>14.1%}")
247
248    best = max(lengths, key=lambda n: (table[n]["morph"]["MRR@10"]
249                                       - table[n]["plain"]["MRR@10"]))
250    p, m = table[best]["plain"]["MRR@10"], table[best]["morph"]["MRR@10"]
251    if p:
252        print(f"\n  largest gain at {best}-term queries: MRR@10 {p:.3f} -> {m:.3f} "
253              f"({(m - p) / p:+.1%})")
254    return table
255
256
257def eval_cross_inflection(corpus, n_docs=1200, top_k=10):
258    """
259    How often does morphology actually decide a query, and how much does it
260    help when it does?
261
262    Experiments 1 and 1b measure the average query, and on the average query
263    the analyser barely moves the needle -- a title word usually appears in
264    the body in the same form, so there is nothing to rescue. The interesting
265    quantity is the size and difficulty of the subset where that is *not*
266    true.
267
268    A query here is a single title word chosen so that
269        - its exact surface form does NOT occur in the article body, but
270        - some body token shares its root.
271    That is precisely the case a plain index cannot serve and a normalised one
272    can. The `coverage` figure below says how often such a word exists at all,
273    which is the honest measure of how much this matters in practice.
274    """
275    from src.retrieve import BM25Index
276    from src.morph import STOPWORDS, stem
277
278    random.seed(SEED)
279    bodies = [r.get("text", "") for r in corpus]
280    doc_ids = list(range(len(corpus)))
281
282    pool = [i for i, r in enumerate(corpus) if len(r.get("text", "")) > 300]
283    sample = random.sample(pool, min(n_docs, len(pool)))
284
285    cases = []
286    for qi in sample:
287        body_tokens = tokenize(corpus[qi]["text"])
288        surface = set(body_tokens)
289        roots = {stem(t) for t in body_tokens}
290        for w in tokenize(corpus[qi].get("title", "")):
291            if w in STOPWORDS or len(w) <= 2:
292                continue
293            if w not in surface and stem(w) in roots:
294                cases.append((qi, w))
295                break
296
297    coverage = len(cases) / len(sample)
298    print(f"  {len(sample)} articles examined")
299    print(f"  {len(cases)} ({coverage:.1%}) contain a headline word that is "
300          f"absent from the body\n  in its surface form but present as a root "
301          f"-- i.e. only a morphological\n  index can match it\n")
302
303    if not cases:
304        return {"coverage": coverage}
305
306    indexes = {m: BM25Index(use_morph=m).build(bodies, doc_ids) for m in (False, True)}
307    out = {}
308    print(f"  {'system':22s} {'R@1':>7s} {'R@10':>7s} {'MRR@10':>8s} {'zero-hit':>10s}")
309    print("  " + "-" * 58)
310    for use_morph, idx in indexes.items():
311        ranks, empty = [], 0
312        for qi, w in cases:
313            hits = idx.search(w, top_k=top_k)
314            if not hits:
315                empty += 1
316            ranks.append(next((h.rank for h in hits if h.doc_id == qi), None))
317        found = [r for r in ranks if r is not None]
318        stats = {
319            "R@1": sum(1 for r in found if r < 1) / len(ranks),
320            "R@10": len(found) / len(ranks),
321            "MRR@10": sum(1 / (r + 1) for r in found) / len(ranks),
322            "zero_hit_rate": empty / len(ranks),
323        }
324        tag = "BM25 + morphology" if use_morph else "BM25 (plain tokens)"
325        out[tag] = stats
326        print(f"  {tag:22s} {stats['R@1']:7.3f} {stats['R@10']:7.3f} "
327              f"{stats['MRR@10']:8.3f} {stats['zero_hit_rate']:9.1%}")
328
329    out["coverage"] = coverage
330    print(f"\n  On this subset the plain index returns nothing for "
331          f"{out['BM25 (plain tokens)']['zero_hit_rate']:.0%} of queries.")
332    print(f"  Weighted over all traffic, the subset is {coverage:.1%} of queries.")
333    return out
334
335
336# ==========================================================================
337# Experiment 2 -- summarization
338# ==========================================================================
339def eval_summarization(corpus, n=300, k=2):
340    from src import summarize as S
341
342    rows = [r for r in corpus if r.get("gold_summary") and len(r.get("text", "")) > 400]
343    random.seed(SEED)
344    rows = random.sample(rows, min(n, len(rows)))
345    if not rows:
346        print("  no gold summaries in corpus (build it from XL-Sum to evaluate)")
347        return {}
348    print(f"  scoring {len(rows)} articles against XL-Sum gold summaries (k={k})\n")
349
350    methods = ["lead", "textrank"]
351    out = {}
352    for method in methods:
353        for use_morph in (False, True):
354            scores = []
355            for r in rows:
356                pred = S.summarize(r["text"], k=k, method=method).text
357                scores.append(rouge_all(pred, r["gold_summary"], use_morph))
358            agg = {m: float(np.mean([s[m] for s in scores])) for m in
359                   ("rouge1", "rouge2", "rougeL")}
360            tag = f"{method}{' +morph' if use_morph else ''}"
361            out[tag] = agg
362
363    print(f"  {'system':18s} {'ROUGE-1':>9s} {'ROUGE-2':>9s} {'ROUGE-L':>9s}")
364    print("  " + "-" * 48)
365    for tag, agg in out.items():
366        print(f"  {tag:18s} {agg['rouge1']:9.4f} {agg['rouge2']:9.4f} {agg['rougeL']:9.4f}")
367    print("\n  (+morph = ROUGE computed over morphologically normalised tokens)")
368    return out
369
370

374def eval_classification(limit=0, model_name=None):
375    import pandas as pd
376    from sklearn.metrics import classification_report
377
378    from src import categorize
379
380    df = pd.read_parquet(config.MAHANEWS_TEST)
381    if limit:
382        df = df.head(limit)
383    texts = df["text"].astype(str).tolist()
384    gold = [config.MAHANEWS_LABELS[int(x)] for x in df["label"]]
385
386    model = model_name or categorize.active_model()
387    print(f"  model: {model}")
388    print(f"  {len(texts)} test headlines\n")
389
390    preds = [p.label for p in categorize.classify(texts, model_name=model)]
391
392    # The 12-class L3Cube model has to be mapped onto the 3-class MahaNews
393    # label space before it can be scored against this test set.
394    if model == config.MODEL_TOPIC:
395        mapping = {"Sports": "sports", "Manoranjan": "entertainment",
396                   "Politics": "state", "Crime": "state", "Auto": "state",
397                   "Bhakti": "state", "Education": "state", "Fashion": "entertainment",
398                   "Health": "state", "International": "state", "Tech": "state",
399                   "Travel": "state"}
400        preds = [mapping.get(p, "state") for p in preds]
401        print("  (12-class zero-shot predictions mapped onto the 3-class"
402              " MahaNews label space)\n")
403
404    acc = sum(p == g for p, g in zip(preds, gold)) / len(gold)
405    print(classification_report(gold, preds, digits=4, zero_division=0))
406    print(f"  accuracy = {acc:.4f}")
407    return {"accuracy": acc}
408

1# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
2"""
3Label XL-Sum with the full models, as training data for the in-browser models.
4
5    python scripts/distill_label.py                      # train + val -> fit, test -> score
6    python scripts/distill_label.py --limit 500          # quick run
7
8The demo page cannot run the MahaBERT models, so it carries small students
9(src/lite.py) trained to reproduce them. This script produces the targets:
10
11  * topic      -- the 12-class topic distribution for every article
12  * sentiment  -- the 3-class distribution for each sentence
13  * entities   -- MahaNER spans for each sentence
14
15Sentences are capped per article so long articles do not dominate. Output is
16one JSON object per article in data/processed/distill_{split}.jsonl.
17"""
18from __future__ import annotations
19
20import argparse
21import json
22import sys
23import time
24from pathlib import Path
25
26import torch
27
28sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent))
29sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8")
30
31import config                                   # noqa: E402
32from src import categorize, models              # noqa: E402
33from src.morph import sent_tokenize             # noqa: E402
34from src.ner import _snap_to_word               # noqa: E402
35
36SPLITS = {"train": config.XLSUM_TRAIN, "val": config.XLSUM_VAL,
37          "test": config.XLSUM_TEST}
38
39
40def load(path: Path, limit: int):
41    rows = []
42    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
43        for line in fh:
44            r = json.loads(line)
45            if len(r.get("text", "")) < 200:
46                continue
47            rows.append(r)
48            if limit and len(rows) >= limit:
49                break
50    return rows
51
52
53def pick_sentences(text: str, cap: int):
54    sents = [s for s in sent_tokenize(text)
55             if len(s.split()) >= 3 and len(s) <= 600]
56    return sents[:cap]
57
58
59@torch.no_grad()
60def ner_batch(texts, batch_size):
61    """Batched MahaNER, returning word-snapped [start, end, label] spans."""
62    tok, mod = models.load_token_classifier(config.MODEL_NER)
63    id2label = mod.config.id2label
64    out = []
65    for i in range(0, len(texts), batch_size):
66        chunk = texts[i:i + batch_size]
67        enc = tok(chunk, return_offsets_mapping=True, truncation=True,
68                  max_length=config.MAX_LEN, padding=True, return_tensors="pt")
69        offsets = enc.pop("offset_mapping").tolist()
70        enc.pop("special_tokens_mask", None)
71        enc = {k: v.to(config.DEVICE) for k, v in enc.items()}
72        labels = mod(**enc).logits.argmax(-1).cpu().tolist()
73        for text, offs, labs in zip(chunk, offsets, labels):
74            spans, cur = [], None
75            for (s, e), lid in zip(offs, labs):
76                if s == e:
77                    continue
78                lab = id2label[lid]
79                if lab == "Other":
80                    cur = None
81                    continue
82                if cur and cur[2] == lab and s - cur[1] <= 1:
83                    cur[1] = e
84                else:
85                    cur = [s, e, lab]
86                    spans.append(cur)
87            snapped = []
88            for s, e, lab in spans:
89                s, e = _snap_to_word(text, s, e)
90                if snapped and snapped[-1][:2] == [s, e]:
91                    continue
92                snapped.append([s, e, lab])
93            out.append(snapped)
94    return out
95
96
97def main():
98    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
99    ap.add_argument("--splits", nargs="+", default=["train", "val", "test"])
100    ap.add_argument("--limit", type=int, default=0, help="articles per split (0 = all)")
101    ap.add_argument("--sent-cap", type=int, default=8)
102    ap.add_argument("--batch", type=int, default=32)
103    args = ap.parse_args()
104
105    for split in args.splits:
106        t0 = time.time()
107        rows = load(SPLITS[split], args.limit)
108        print(f"[{split}] {len(rows)} articles on {config.DEVICE}", flush=True)
109
110        topics = categorize.classify([f"{r['title']}. {r['text']}" for r in rows],
111                                     batch_size=args.batch)
112        print(f"  topics      ({time.time() - t0:.0f}s)", flush=True)
113
114        sents_per_doc = [pick_sentences(r["text"], args.sent_cap) for r in rows]
115        # The title is labelled too: pasted input often starts with one.
116        flat = [s for r, ss in zip(rows, sents_per_doc) for s in [r["title"], *ss]]
117
118        sent_scores = []
119        tok, mod = models.load_classifier(config.MODEL_SENTIMENT)
120        id2label = mod.config.id2label
121        order = [id2label[j] for j in range(len(id2label))]
122        with torch.no_grad():
123            for i in range(0, len(flat), args.batch):
124                chunk = flat[i:i + args.batch]
125                enc = tok(chunk, padding=True, truncation=True,
126                          max_length=config.MAX_LEN, return_tensors="pt").to(config.DEVICE)
127                probs = mod(**enc).logits.float().softmax(-1).cpu().tolist()
128                sent_scores.extend(
129                    [{lab: round(p[j], 4) for j, lab in enumerate(order)} for p in probs])
130        print(f"  sentiment   {len(flat)} sentences ({time.time() - t0:.0f}s)", flush=True)
131
132        spans = ner_batch(flat, args.batch)
133        print(f"  entities    ({time.time() - t0:.0f}s)", flush=True)
134
135        out = config.PROCESSED / f"distill_{split}.jsonl"
136        k = 0
137        with open(out, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
138            for r, pred, ss in zip(rows, topics, sents_per_doc):
139                n = len(ss) + 1
140                fh.write(json.dumps({
141                    "id": r["id"], "title": r["title"], "text": r["text"],
142                    "topic": {lab: round(v, 4) for lab, v in pred.all_scores.items()},
143                    "sentences": [{"s": s, "sent": sc, "ner": sp} for s, sc, sp in
144                                  zip(flat[k:k + n], sent_scores[k:k + n], spans[k:k + n])],
145                }, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
146                k += n
147        print(f"  wrote {out}  ({time.time() - t0:.0f}s)", flush=True)
148
149
150if __name__ == "__main__":
151    main()

1# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
2"""
3Train the in-browser student models (src/lite.py) on the full models' output.
4
5    python scripts/distill_label.py      # label XL-Sum with the full models
6    python scripts/train_lite.py         # fit, score on test, write app/lite_models.json
7
8Each student is a linear softmax model trained against the teacher's
9probabilities (soft targets), using torch EmbeddingBag so the sparse features
10never become a dense matrix. Weights are then rounded to small integers times
11one scale per model -- that is what the page embeds -- and the *rounded*
12models are what get scored, so the agreement figures describe exactly what
13ships.
14
15Agreement is measured against the teacher on the XL-Sum test split, which the
16students never see:
17
18  * topic      -- top-1 label matches the 12-class topic model
19  * sentiment  -- sentence label matches the sentiment model; also the
20                  document tone after the same length-weighted aggregation
21  * entities   -- span-level precision / recall / F1 against MahaNER
22"""
23from __future__ import annotations
24
25import argparse
26import base64
27import json
28import math
29import sys
30import time
31from collections import Counter
32from pathlib import Path
33
34import torch
35
36sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent))
37sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8")
38
39import config                                              # noqa: E402
40from src import lite                                       # noqa: E402
41
42torch.manual_seed(0)
43
44
45def load(split):
46    path = config.PROCESSED / f"distill_{split}.jsonl"
47    if not path.exists():
48        sys.exit(f"{path} missing -- run scripts/distill_label.py first")
49    return [json.loads(l) for l in open(path, encoding="utf-8")]
50
51
52# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
53# Generic sparse softmax regression
54# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
55def fit_softmax(rows, targets, n_feats, n_classes, *, epochs, lr, l2,
56                batch=256):
57    """
58    rows: list of (feature_ids, feature_values); targets: list of prob lists.
59    Returns (W [n_feats x n_classes], b [n_classes]) as float tensors.
60    """
61    emb = torch.nn.EmbeddingBag(n_feats, n_classes, mode="sum")
62    torch.nn.init.zeros_(emb.weight)
63    bias = torch.nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(n_classes))
64    opt = torch.optim.Adam(list(emb.parameters()) + [bias], lr=lr)
65    y_all = torch.tensor(targets, dtype=torch.float32)
66    order = list(range(len(rows)))
67
68    for ep in range(epochs):
69        g = torch.Generator().manual_seed(ep)
70        perm = torch.randperm(len(order), generator=g).tolist()
71        total = 0.0
72        for i in range(0, len(perm), batch):
73            idx = perm[i:i + batch]
74            ids, vals, offs = [], [], []
75            for r in idx:
76                offs.append(len(ids))
77                ids.extend(rows[r][0])
78                vals.extend(rows[r][1])
79            logits = emb(torch.tensor(ids, dtype=torch.long),
80                         torch.tensor(offs, dtype=torch.long),
81                         per_sample_weights=torch.tensor(vals, dtype=torch.float32)) + bias
82            loss = -(y_all[idx] * logits.log_softmax(-1)).sum(-1).mean()
83            loss = loss + l2 * emb.weight.pow(2).sum() / len(rows)
84            opt.zero_grad()
85            loss.backward()
86            opt.step()
87            total += loss.item() * len(idx)
88        print(f"    epoch {ep + 1}/{epochs}  loss {total / len(rows):.4f}", flush=True)
89    return emb.weight.detach(), bias.detach()
90
91
92def quantize(W, levels=127):
93    """
94    int8 weights plus one scale, packed row-major and base64-encoded -- about
95    a third of the size of a JSON list of numbers.
96    """
97    scale = float(W.abs().max()) / levels or 1.0
98    q = torch.round(W / scale).clamp(-levels, levels).to(torch.int8)
99    return base64.b64encode(q.numpy().tobytes()).decode("ascii"), scale
100
101
102# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
103# Topic
104# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
105def train_topic(train, max_vocab):
106    labels = sorted(train[0]["topic"])
107    docs = [lite.topic_terms(r["title"], r["text"]) for r in train]
108    df = Counter(t for d in docs for t in set(d))
109    vocab = [t for t, c in df.most_common(max_vocab) if c >= 3]
110    index = {t: i for i, t in enumerate(vocab)}
111    n = len(docs)
112    idf = [round(math.log((1 + n) / (1 + df[t])) + 1.0, 4) for t in vocab]
113
114    rows = []
115    for d in docs:
116        tf = Counter(t for t in d if t in index)
117        vec = {t: (1 + math.log(c)) * idf[index[t]] for t, c in tf.items()}
118        norm = math.sqrt(sum(v * v for v in vec.values())) or 1.0
119        rows.append(([index[t] for t in vec], [v / norm for v in vec.values()]))
120    targets = [[r["topic"][l] for l in labels] for r in train]
121    print(f"  topic: {len(vocab):,} terms, {len(rows):,} articles")
122    W, b = fit_softmax(rows, targets, len(vocab), len(labels),
123                       epochs=12, lr=0.05, l2=1e-4)
124    Wq, scale = quantize(W)
125    return {"labels": labels, "terms": vocab, "idf": idf, "W": Wq,
126            "b": [round(float(x), 4) for x in b], "scale": scale,
127            "max_tokens": lite.TOPIC_MAX_TOKENS}
128
129
130# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
131# Sentiment
132# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
133def train_sentiment(train, max_feats):
134    labels = ["Negative", "Neutral", "Positive"]
135    sents = [s for r in train for s in r["sentences"]]
136    feats = [set(lite.sentiment_features(s["s"])) for s in sents]
137    cnt = Counter(f for fs in feats for f in fs)
138    vocab = [f for f, c in cnt.most_common(max_feats) if c >= 3]
139    index = {f: i for i, f in enumerate(vocab)}
140    rows = []
141    for fs in feats:
142        known = sorted(f for f in fs if f in index)
143        inv = 1.0 / math.sqrt(len(known)) if known else 0.0
144        rows.append(([index[f] for f in known], [inv] * len(known)))
145    targets = [[s["sent"][l] for l in labels] for s in sents]
146    print(f"  sentiment: {len(vocab):,} features, {len(rows):,} sentences")
147    W, b = fit_softmax(rows, targets, len(vocab), len(labels),
148                       epochs=8, lr=0.03, l2=1e-4, batch=512)
149    Wq, scale = quantize(W)
150    return {"labels": labels, "feats": vocab, "W": Wq,
151            "b": [round(float(x), 4) for x in b], "scale": scale}
152
153
154# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
155# Entities
156# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
157def word_labels(text, spans):
158    offs = lite.words(text)
159    out = []
160    for s, e in offs:
161        lab = "O"
162        for a, z, l in spans:
163            if a <= s and e <= z:
164                lab = l
165                break
166        out.append(lab)
167    return [text[s:e] for s, e in offs], out
168
169
170def train_ner(train, max_feats, keep):
171    labels = lite.NER_LABELS
172    lid = {l: i for i, l in enumerate(labels)}
173    seqs = []
174    for r in train:
175        for s in r["sentences"]:
176            toks, labs = word_labels(s["s"], s["ner"])
177            if toks:
178                seqs.append((toks, labs))
179
180    # Teacher forcing: previous-label features use the teacher's labels.
181    examples, cnt = [], Counter()
182    for toks, labs in seqs:
183        for i in range(len(toks)):
184            prev = labs[i - 1] if i > 0 else "O"
185            prev2 = labs[i - 2] if i > 1 else "O"
186            fs = lite.ner_features(toks, i, prev, prev2)
187            examples.append((fs, lid[labs[i]]))
188            cnt.update(fs)
189    vocab = [f for f, c in cnt.most_common(max_feats) if c >= 2]
190    index = {f: i for i, f in enumerate(vocab)}
191    rows = []
192    for fs, _ in examples:
193        known = [index[f] for f in fs if f in index]
194        rows.append((known, [1.0] * len(known)))
195    targets = [[1.0 if j == y else 0.0 for j in range(len(labels))] for _, y in examples]
196    print(f"  entities: {len(vocab):,} features, {len(rows):,} words, "
197          f"{sum(1 for _, y in examples if y):,} inside entities")
198    W, b = fit_softmax(rows, targets, len(vocab), len(labels),
199                       epochs=6, lr=0.05, l2=1e-5, batch=1024)
200
201    # Keep the features that move the most decisions: weight spread times how
202    # often the feature fires. Spread alone keeps rare, memorised features
203    # and drops common decisive ones (the weights that say "आहे" is not a
204    # name), which halves precision at the same size.
205    spread = (W.max(1).values - W.min(1).values)
206    freq = torch.tensor([cnt[f] for f in vocab], dtype=torch.float32)
207    order = torch.argsort(spread * freq, descending=True)[:keep].tolist()
208    order.sort()
209    Wk = W[order]
210    Wq, scale = quantize(Wk)
211    return {"labels": labels, "feats": [vocab[i] for i in order], "W": Wq,
212            "b": [round(float(x), 4) for x in b], "scale": scale}
213
214
215# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
216# Scoring the shipped (rounded) models
217# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
218def score(model: lite.Lite, test):
219    top = sum(max(model.topic(r["title"], r["text"]).items(), key=lambda kv: kv[1])[0]
220              == max(r["topic"], key=r["topic"].get) for r in test)
221
222    s_ok = s_n = d_ok = 0
223    for r in test:
224        pols, weights = [], []
225        for s in r["sentences"]:
226            p = model.sentence_sentiment(s["s"])
227            s_ok += max(p, key=p.get) == max(s["sent"], key=s["sent"].get)
228            s_n += 1
229        # Document tone over the article's sentences, both sides aggregated
230        # the same way (length-weighted expected polarity).
231        def tone(get):
232            num = den = 0.0
233            for s in r["sentences"]:
234                p = get(s)
235                w = max(len(s["s"]), 1)
236                num += w * sum(lite.POLARITY[k] * v for k, v in p.items())
237                den += w
238            pol = num / den if den else 0.0
239            return "Positive" if pol > 0.15 else "Negative" if pol < -0.15 else "Neutral"
240        d_ok += tone(lambda s: model.sentence_sentiment(s["s"])) == tone(lambda s: s["sent"])
241
242    tp = fp = fn = 0
243    for r in test:
244        for s in r["sentences"]:
245            gold = {tuple(x) for x in s["ner"]}
246            pred = set(model.entities(s["s"]))
247            tp += len(gold & pred)
248            fp += len(pred - gold)
249            fn += len(gold - pred)
250    p = tp / max(tp + fp, 1)
251    rc = tp / max(tp + fn, 1)
252    return {
253        "test_articles": len(test),
254        "topic_top1_agreement": round(top / len(test), 4),
255        "sentiment_sentence_agreement": round(s_ok / max(s_n, 1), 4),
256        "sentiment_document_agreement": round(d_ok / len(test), 4),
257        "ner_precision": round(p, 4), "ner_recall": round(rc, 4),
258        "ner_f1": round(2 * p * rc / max(p + rc, 1e-9), 4),
259    }
260
261
262def main():
263    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
264    ap.add_argument("--topic-vocab", type=int, default=20000)
265    ap.add_argument("--sent-feats", type=int, default=40000)
266    ap.add_argument("--ner-feats", type=int, default=400000)
267    ap.add_argument("--ner-keep", type=int, default=40000)
268    ap.add_argument("--out", default=str(lite.LITE_MODELS))
269    args = ap.parse_args()
270
271    t0 = time.time()
272    train = load("train") + load("val")
273    test = load("test")
274    print(f"{len(train):,} training articles, {len(test):,} test articles")
275
276    data = {
277        "topic": train_topic(train, args.topic_vocab),
278        "sentiment": train_sentiment(train, args.sent_feats),
279        "ner": train_ner(train, args.ner_feats, args.ner_keep),
280    }
281    print(f"trained ({time.time() - t0:.0f}s); scoring the rounded models on test...")
282    data["agreement"] = score(lite.Lite(data), test)
283    for k, v in data["agreement"].items():
284        print(f"  {k:32s} {v}")
285
286    out = Path(args.out)
287    out.write_text(json.dumps(data, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":")),
288                   encoding="utf-8")
289    print(f"wrote {out}  ({out.stat().st_size / 1024:.0f} KB, {time.time() - t0:.0f}s)")
290
291
292if __name__ == "__main__":
293    main()

1# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
2"""
3Export everything the demo page needs into one JSON file.
4
5    python scripts/export_demo.py --docs 400 --showcase 8
6
7Two things are exported, and the distinction matters:
8
9  * REAL PIPELINE OUTPUT -- topics, entities, sentiment, summaries and
10    translations that the actual models produced, copied verbatim out of
11    data/processed/corpus.jsonl. The demo page does not re-run any model; it
12    displays what the pipeline already computed.
13
14  * THE ANALYSER'S RULE TABLES -- the suffix inventory, stopword list and
15    exception map are dumped straight from src/morph.py so the JavaScript
16    port on the page runs the *same* rules rather than a hand-retyped copy
17    that could silently drift out of sync.
18
19Translation is done here rather than in build_corpus so only the handful of
20showcase articles pay the NLLB cost. Run with CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES= to keep it
21off a GPU that is busy training.
22"""
23from __future__ import annotations
24
25import argparse
26import json
27import sys
28from collections import Counter, defaultdict
29from pathlib import Path
30
31sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent))
32sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8")
33
34import config                       # noqa: E402
35from src import morph               # noqa: E402
36from src.lite import LITE_MODELS    # noqa: E402
37from src.ner import merge_aliases   # noqa: E402
38
39
40def morph_tables() -> dict:
41    """Dump the analyser's rules so the JS port stays in lockstep."""
42    def flat(table):
43        return [[t[0], t[1], t[2] if len(t) > 2 else ""] for t in table]
44
45    return {
46        "clitics": flat(morph.CLITICS),
47        "postpositions": flat(morph.POSTPOSITIONS),
48        "verb": flat(morph.VERB_SUFFIXES),
49        "case": flat(morph.CASE_NUMBER),
50        "stopwords": sorted(morph.STOPWORDS),
51        "exceptions": morph.EXCEPTIONS,
52        "marks": "".join(sorted(morph._MARKS)),
53        "finalMatras": "".join(sorted(morph._FINAL_MATRAS)),
54        "minStem": morph.MIN_STEM,
55        "maxStrips": morph.MAX_STRIPS,
56        "virama": morph.VIRAMA,
57    }
58
59
60def pick_showcase(corpus, n):
61    """Spread the showcase across topics, preferring entity-rich articles."""
62    by_topic = defaultdict(list)
63    for r in corpus:
64        by_topic[r.get("topic", "?")].append(r)
65
66    def richness(r):
67        return sum(len(v) for v in (r.get("entities") or {}).values())
68
69    picks, topics = [], sorted(by_topic, key=lambda t: -len(by_topic[t]))
70    while len(picks) < n and topics:
71        for t in list(topics):
72            pool = [r for r in by_topic[t]
73                    if 400 < len(r.get("text", "")) < 6000 and richness(r) >= 4]
74            pool.sort(key=richness, reverse=True)
75            pool = [r for r in pool if r not in picks]
76            if pool:
77                picks.append(pool[0])
78            else:
79                topics.remove(t)
80            if len(picks) >= n:
81                break
82    return picks[:n]
83
84
85def slim(rec, keep_text=False):
86    out = {
87        "id": rec.get("id"),
88        "title": rec.get("title", ""),
89        "summary": rec.get("summary", ""),
90        "topic": rec.get("topic", ""),
91        "topic_score": round(float(rec.get("topic_score", 0)), 3),
92        "sentiment": rec.get("sentiment", ""),
93        "polarity": round(float(rec.get("polarity", 0)), 3),
94        "entities": rec.get("entities") or {},
95        "url": rec.get("url", ""),
96        "tokens": rec.get("tokens", 0),
97        "inflected_ratio": round(float(rec.get("inflected_ratio", 0)), 3),
98    }
99    if keep_text:
100        out["text"] = rec.get("text", "")
101        out["gold_summary"] = rec.get("gold_summary", "")
102        out["topic_scores"] = {k: round(float(v), 4)
103                               for k, v in (rec.get("topic_scores") or {}).items()}
104        out["sentiment_distribution"] = rec.get("sentiment_distribution") or {}
105    return out
106
107
108def main():
109    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
110    ap.add_argument("--docs", type=int, default=400, help="docs in the search index")
111    ap.add_argument("--showcase", type=int, default=8)
112    ap.add_argument("--no-translate", action="store_true")
113    ap.add_argument("--out", default=str(config.OUTPUTS / "demo_data.json"))
114    args = ap.parse_args()
115
116    if not LITE_MODELS.exists():
117        sys.exit(f"{LITE_MODELS} missing -- run scripts/train_lite.py first")
118    corpus = [json.loads(l) for l in open(config.CORPUS_JSONL, encoding="utf-8")]
119    print(f"corpus: {len(corpus)} docs")
120
121    showcase = pick_showcase(corpus, args.showcase)
122    print(f"showcase: {len(showcase)} articles "
123          f"({', '.join(r['topic'] for r in showcase)})")
124
125    # Search index: the showcase articles plus a topic-spread sample.
126    chosen = {id(r): r for r in showcase}
127    per_topic = defaultdict(int)
128    cap = max(1, args.docs // max(len(set(r.get('topic') for r in corpus)), 1))
129    for r in corpus:
130        if len(chosen) >= args.docs:
131            break
132        t = r.get("topic", "?")
133        if id(r) in chosen or per_topic[t] >= cap or len(r.get("text", "")) < 300:
134            continue
135        chosen[id(r)] = r
136        per_topic[t] += 1
137    for r in corpus:                      # top up if caps left us short
138        if len(chosen) >= args.docs:
139            break
140        if id(r) not in chosen and len(r.get("text", "")) >= 300:
141            chosen[id(r)] = r
142    docs = list(chosen.values())
143    print(f"search index: {len(docs)} docs")
144
145    # Translation of the showcase only.
146    if not args.no_translate:
147        from src import translate as mt
148        print(f"translating {len(showcase)} showcase articles on {config.DEVICE}...")
149        titles = mt.translate([r["title"] for r in showcase])
150        summaries = mt.translate([r["summary"][:700] for r in showcase])
151        for r, t, s in zip(showcase, titles, summaries):
152            r["_title_en"], r["_summary_en"] = t, s
153        print("  done")
154
155    show_out = []
156    for r in showcase:
157        d = slim(r, keep_text=True)
158        d["title_en"] = r.get("_title_en", "")
159        d["summary_en"] = r.get("_summary_en", "")
160        show_out.append(d)
161
162    # Corpus-level aggregates, computed over the whole 3,000 not the sample.
163    ent_buckets = defaultdict(Counter)
164    for r in corpus:
165        for label, vals in (r.get("entities") or {}).items():
166            for v in vals:
167                ent_buckets[label][v] += 1
168    top_entities = {
169        label: merge_aliases(c).most_common(12)
170        for label, c in ent_buckets.items()
171        if label in ("Person", "Organization", "Location")
172    }
173
174    tone_by_topic = defaultdict(lambda: Counter())
175    for r in corpus:
176        tone_by_topic[r.get("topic", "?")][r.get("sentiment", "Neutral")] += 1
177
178    payload = {
179        "meta": {
180            "corpus_size": len(corpus),
181            "index_size": len(docs),
182            "mean_inflected_ratio": round(
183                sum(r.get("inflected_ratio", 0) for r in corpus) / len(corpus), 4),
184            "source": "XL-Sum Marathi (BBC Marathi)",
185        },
186        "morph": morph_tables(),
187        "showcase": show_out,
188        "docs": [slim(r) for r in docs],
189        "topics": Counter(r.get("topic", "?") for r in corpus).most_common(),
190        "sentiment": Counter(r.get("sentiment", "?") for r in corpus).most_common(),
191        "tone_by_topic": {k: dict(v) for k, v in tone_by_topic.items()},
192        "top_entities": top_entities,
193        # The in-browser students (src/lite.py), so pasted text can be
194        # analysed with no Python -- with their measured agreement.
195        "lite": json.loads(LITE_MODELS.read_text(encoding="utf-8")),
196    }
197
198    out = Path(args.out)
199    out.write_text(json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8")
200    print(f"wrote {out}  ({out.stat().st_size / 1024:.0f} KB)")
201
202
203if __name__ == "__main__":
204    main()

Assembles the single-file demo page.

1# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
2"""
3Assemble the standalone demo page, Marathi-NLP-Demo.html.
4
5    python scripts/export_demo.py        # data + model weights -> outputs/demo_data.json
6    python scripts/build_demo_page.py    # -> Marathi-NLP-Demo.html
7    python scripts/verify_demo.py        # JavaScript vs Python parity
8
9The page is a single self-contained HTML file: the JSON payload goes into a
10<script type="application/json"> tag rather than being fetched, and the
11engine (app/demo_engine.js) is inlined, so the page works offline and can be
12emailed or opened from a pendrive.
13"""
14from __future__ import annotations
15
16import json
17import sys
18from pathlib import Path
19
20sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent))
21sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8")
22
23import config  # noqa: E402
24
25TEMPLATE = config.ROOT / "app" / "demo_template.html"
26ENGINE = config.ROOT / "app" / "demo_engine.js"
27DATA = config.OUTPUTS / "demo_data.json"
28OUT = config.ROOT / "Marathi-NLP-Demo.html"
29
30
31def main():
32    if not DATA.exists():
33        sys.exit("run scripts/export_demo.py first")
34    payload = json.loads(DATA.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
35
36    # A literal </script> inside the JSON would close the tag early;
37    # escaping the slash keeps the JSON valid but hides it from the
38    # HTML parser.
39    blob = json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":")) \
40        .replace("</", "<" + chr(92) + "/")
41    engine = ENGINE.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
42    if "</script" in engine:
43        sys.exit("demo_engine.js must not contain '</script'")
44
45    html = TEMPLATE.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
46    for marker in ("__DATA__", "/*__ENGINE__*/"):
47        if html.count(marker) != 1:
48            sys.exit(f"template must contain {marker} exactly once")
49    html = html.replace("__DATA__", blob).replace("/*__ENGINE__*/", engine)
50    OUT.write_text(html, encoding="utf-8")
51    print(f"wrote {OUT}  ({OUT.stat().st_size/1024:.0f} KB)")
52
53
54if __name__ == "__main__":
55    main()

1# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
2"""
3Check that the demo page's JavaScript gives the same answers as the Python.
4
5    python scripts/verify_demo.py            (needs node on PATH)
6    python scripts/verify_demo.py --n 1000   # more test articles
7
8The page re-implements the analyser, TextRank and the three in-browser
9students (src/lite.py) in JavaScript. That port is only trustworthy if it
10agrees with the Python, so this script pulls the engine and the embedded
11payload *out of the built page itself* -- i.e. exactly what ships -- runs
12them under Node, and compares, stage by stage:
13
14  I  roots of every Devanagari word in the page's search corpus
15  E  TextRank summaries of held-out XL-Sum test articles
16  D  topic probabilities                    (same label, |diff| < 1e-6)
17  F  sentence sentiment probabilities       (same label, |diff| < 1e-6)
18  G  entity spans and the grouped entity lists
19     and the whole pipeline() output
20"""
21from __future__ import annotations
22
23import argparse
24import json
25import re
26import subprocess
27import sys
28import tempfile
29from pathlib import Path
30
31sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent))
32sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8")
33
34import config                                 # noqa: E402
35from src import lite                          # noqa: E402
36from src.morph import sent_tokenize, stem     # noqa: E402
37from src.summarize import summarize           # noqa: E402
38
39PAGE = config.ROOT / "Marathi-NLP-Demo.html"
40TOL = 1e-6
41
42RUNNER = r"""
43const fs = require("fs"), vm = require("vm");
44const [enginePath, payloadPath, casesPath] = process.argv.slice(2);
45const ctx = { atob: s => Buffer.from(s, "base64").toString("latin1") };
46vm.createContext(ctx);
47vm.runInContext(fs.readFileSync(enginePath, "utf8") + "\nthis.makeEngine = makeEngine;", ctx);
48const E = ctx.makeEngine(JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(payloadPath, "utf8")));
49const C = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(casesPath, "utf8"));
50const out = {
51  stems: C.words.map(w => E.stem(w)),
52  summaries: C.docs.map(d => E.summarize(d.text, 3).join(" ")),
53  topics: C.docs.map(d => E.topic(d.title, d.text)),
54  sentiment: C.sentences.map(s => E.sentenceSentiment(s)),
55  spans: C.sentences.map(s => E.entitySpans(s).map(([a, b, l]) => [s.slice(a, b), l])),
56  pipeline: C.docs.map(d => {
57    const r = E.pipeline(d.title, d.text);
58    return { topic_scores: r.topic_scores, summary: r.summary, entities: r.entities,
59             sentiment: r.sentiment, polarity: r.polarity,
60             sentiment_distribution: r.sentiment_distribution };
61  }),
62};
63process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify(out));
64"""
65
66
67def extract(html: str):
68    m = re.search(r'<script id="payload" type="application/json">(.*?)</script>', html, re.S)
69    if not m:
70        sys.exit("no embedded payload found in the page")
71    payload = json.loads(m.group(1).replace("<" + chr(92) + "/", "</"))
72    engines = [s for s in re.findall(r"<script>(.*?)</script>", html, re.S)
73               if "function makeEngine" in s]
74    if len(engines) != 1:
75        sys.exit("could not find the inlined engine in the page")
76    return payload, engines[0]
77
78
79def close(a: dict, b: dict) -> bool:
80    return (max(a, key=a.get) == max(b, key=b.get)
81            and all(abs(a[k] - b[k]) < TOL for k in a))
82
83
84def main():
85    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
86    ap.add_argument("--n", type=int, default=300, help="held-out test articles")
87    args = ap.parse_args()
88
89    if not PAGE.exists():
90        sys.exit(f"{PAGE} not found -- run scripts/build_demo_page.py first")
91    payload, engine = extract(PAGE.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
92    model = lite.Lite(payload["lite"])
93
94    words = set()
95    for rec in payload["docs"]:
96        words.update(re.findall(r"[ऀ-ॿ]+", rec["title"] + " " + rec["summary"]))
97    words = sorted(words)
98
99    docs = []
100    with open(config.XLSUM_TEST, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
101        for line in fh:
102            r = json.loads(line)
103            if len(r["text"]) >= 200:
104                docs.append({"title": r["title"], "text": r["text"]})
105            if len(docs) >= args.n:
106                break
107    sentences = [s for d in docs for s in [d["title"], *sent_tokenize(d["text"])[:6]]]
108    print(f"checking {len(words):,} words, {len(docs)} articles, "
109          f"{len(sentences):,} sentences")
110
111    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as td:
112        td = Path(td)
113        (td / "engine.js").write_text(engine, encoding="utf-8")
114        (td / "payload.json").write_text(json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8")
115        (td / "cases.json").write_text(json.dumps(
116            {"words": words, "docs": docs, "sentences": sentences}, ensure_ascii=False),
117            encoding="utf-8")
118        (td / "run.js").write_text(RUNNER, encoding="utf-8")
119        try:
120            r = subprocess.run(["node", str(td / "run.js"), str(td / "engine.js"),
121                                str(td / "payload.json"), str(td / "cases.json")],
122                               capture_output=True, text=True, encoding="utf-8")
123        except FileNotFoundError:
124            sys.exit("node not found on PATH -- install Node.js to run this check")
125    if r.returncode != 0:
126        sys.exit("node failed:\n" + r.stderr)
127    js = json.loads(r.stdout)
128
129    checks = {}
130
131    def record(name, bad, total, example=None):
132        checks[name] = (bad, total)
133        if bad and example:
134            print(f"    first mismatch in {name}: {example}")
135
136    bad = [(w, j) for w, j in zip(words, js["stems"]) if stem(w) != j]
137    record("I  roots", len(bad), len(words), bad[:1])
138
139    py_sum = [summarize(d["text"], k=3).text for d in docs]
140    bad = [i for i, (p, j) in enumerate(zip(py_sum, js["summaries"])) if p != j]
141    record("E  summaries", len(bad), len(docs), bad[:1])
142
143    bad = [i for i, (d, j) in enumerate(zip(docs, js["topics"]))
144           if not close(model.topic(d["title"], d["text"]), j)]
145    record("D  topic", len(bad), len(docs), bad[:1])
146
147    bad = [s for s, j in zip(sentences, js["sentiment"])
148           if not close(model.sentence_sentiment(s), j)]
149    record("F  sentiment", len(bad), len(sentences), bad[:1])
150
151    bad = []
152    for s, j in zip(sentences, js["spans"]):
153        py = [[s[a:b], lab] for a, b, lab in model.entities(s)]
154        if py != j:
155            bad.append((s, py, j))
156    record("G  entity spans", len(bad), len(sentences), bad[:1])
157
158    bad = []
159    for d, j in zip(docs, js["pipeline"]):
160        p = lite.analyse(model, d["title"], d["text"])
161        same = (p["summary"] == j["summary"] and p["entities"] == j["entities"]
162                and p["sentiment"] == j["sentiment"]
163                and p["sentiment_distribution"] == j["sentiment_distribution"]
164                and abs(p["polarity"] - j["polarity"]) < TOL
165                and close(p["topic_scores"], j["topic_scores"]))
166        if not same:
167            bad.append(d["title"])
168    record("   whole pipeline", len(bad), len(docs), bad[:1])
169
170    failed = False
171    for name, (b, n) in checks.items():
172        print(f"  {name:18s} {n - b:>6,} / {n:,} identical")
173        failed |= b > 0
174    if failed:
175        sys.exit("PARITY FAILED: the page disagrees with the Python modules")
176    print("PARITY OK -- the page computes exactly what the Python modules compute")
177
178
179if __name__ == "__main__":
180    main()

1# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
2"""
3Marathi News Intelligence -- Streamlit dashboard.
4
5    streamlit run app/dashboard.py
6
7Five tabs, one per part of the pipeline:
8  Search      -- morphology-aware hybrid retrieval over the enriched corpus (C)
9  Overview    -- topic and sentiment distribution, most-covered entities (D/F/G)
10  Entity tone -- how a given person/party is being covered (F over G)
11  Morphology  -- the analyser, and a side-by-side plain vs morph search (I)
12  Analyse     -- run the full pipeline on pasted text or live RSS (A/D/E/F/G)
13
14Heavy objects are cached: the corpus and indexes load once per session, and
15each transformer is held by src.models for the process lifetime.
16"""

64def load_plain_index(corpus_len: int):
65    """Morphology-free index, built lazily for the side-by-side comparison."""
66    corpus = load_corpus()
67    texts = [f"{r.get('title','')} {r.get('text','')}" for r in corpus]

72def entity_counts():

74    buckets = defaultdict(Counter)

76        for label, vals in (r.get("entities") or {}).items():
77            for v in vals:

1# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
2"""
3Local model server for the demo page.
4
5    python app/server.py              # http://127.0.0.1:8765
6
7The demo page (Marathi-NLP-Demo.html) always works on its own, using the
8small in-browser models from src/lite.py. When this server is running, the
9page detects it and sends pasted text here instead, so the full pipeline --
10MahaBERT topic model, MahaNER, the sentiment model and NLLB-200 -- analyses
11it. Nothing else changes on the page.
12
13Endpoints (JSON):
14  GET  /api/health                     -> {"ok": true, "device": ...}
15  POST /api/analyse  {title, text, translate}
16                                       -> the pipeline's Document as a dict
17  POST /api/translate {texts: [...]}   -> {"translations": [...]}
18
19Standard library only. It listens on 127.0.0.1, so it is reachable from this
20machine and nowhere else.
21"""
22from __future__ import annotations
23
24import json
25import os
26import sys
27import threading
28from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer
29from pathlib import Path
30
31sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent))
32sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8")
33
34import config  # noqa: E402
35
36HOST = "127.0.0.1"
37PORT = int(os.environ.get("MNIP_PORT", 8765))
38MAX_CHARS = 20000
39
40# The models are not thread-safe to load concurrently, and one request at a
41# time is plenty for a demo.
42_LOCK = threading.Lock()
43
44
45def analyse(payload: dict) -> dict:
46    from src.pipeline import process
47    title = str(payload.get("title") or "")[:1000]
48    text = str(payload.get("text") or "")[:MAX_CHARS]
49    if not text.strip():
50        raise ValueError("text is empty")
51    with _LOCK:
52        doc = process(title, text, translate=bool(payload.get("translate")))
53    return doc.to_dict()
54
55
56def translate(payload: dict) -> dict:
57    from src import translate as mt
58    texts = [str(t)[:2000] for t in (payload.get("texts") or [])][:40]
59    if not texts:
60        return {"translations": []}
61    with _LOCK:
62        return {"translations": mt.translate(texts)}
63
64
65class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
66    server_version = "MarathiNLP/1.0"
67
68    def _headers(self, status=200, body_len=0):
69        self.send_response(status)
70        self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json; charset=utf-8")
71        # The page is usually opened from file://, whose origin is "null".
72        self.send_header("Access-Control-Allow-Origin", "*")
73        self.send_header("Access-Control-Allow-Methods", "GET, POST, OPTIONS")
74        self.send_header("Access-Control-Allow-Headers", "Content-Type")
75        # Chrome's Private Network Access preflight for pages on https://.
76        self.send_header("Access-Control-Allow-Private-Network", "true")
77        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(body_len))
78        self.end_headers()
79
80    def _json(self, obj, status=200):
81        body = json.dumps(obj, ensure_ascii=False).encode("utf-8")
82        self._headers(status, len(body))
83        self.wfile.write(body)
84
85    def do_OPTIONS(self):  # noqa: N802
86        self._headers(204)
87
88    def do_GET(self):  # noqa: N802
89        if self.path.rstrip("/") == "/api/health":
90            self._json({"ok": True, "device": config.DEVICE,
91                        "models": {"topic": config.MODEL_TOPIC,
92                                   "ner": config.MODEL_NER,
93                                   "sentiment": config.MODEL_SENTIMENT,
94                                   "translation": config.MODEL_TRANSLATE}})
95        else:
96            self._json({"error": "not found"}, 404)
97
98    def do_POST(self):  # noqa: N802
99        routes = {"/api/analyse": analyse, "/api/translate": translate}
100        fn = routes.get(self.path.rstrip("/"))
101        if fn is None:
102            return self._json({"error": "not found"}, 404)
103        try:
104            n = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length") or 0)
105            payload = json.loads(self.rfile.read(n) or b"{}")
106            self._json(fn(payload))
107        except ValueError as exc:
108            self._json({"error": str(exc)}, 400)
109        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
110            self._json({"error": f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"}, 500)
111
112    def log_message(self, fmt, *args):
113        sys.stderr.write("  %s %s\n" % (self.command, self.path))
114
115
116def main():
117    print(f"Marathi NLP model server on http://{HOST}:{PORT}  (device: {config.DEVICE})")
118    print("Open Marathi-NLP-Demo.html -- it will switch to the full models.")
119    print("Models load on the first request (the first one takes a while).")
120    ThreadingHTTPServer((HOST, PORT), Handler).serve_forever()
121
122
123if __name__ == "__main__":
124    main()
